The crossover flavor $N^{*}(Ω)$ falls monotonically at fixed temperature (a corollary). The critical flavor number is unchanged by rotation at $T=0$ (theorem). Together these results set the finite-temperature reference for the model.

papers.title: Mapping the Contracting Corona in GS 1354-64 with Insight-HXMT and XRISM: Evolving X-ray Lags and Quenched Reflection across a Complete State Transition
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive broadband spectro-temporal analysis of the dynamically confirmed Galactic black hole transient GS 1354-64 during its 2025-26 outburst, using near-simultaneous observations from Insight-HXMT and XRISM. The high spectral resolution of the XRISM-Resolve microcalorimeter, coupled with the high-cadence broadband coverage of Insight-HXMT, reveals a dramatic evolution in the inner accretion geometry. During the early hard-intermediate state, the spectrum was dominated by a hot Comptonizing corona accompanied by relativistically broadened reflection features. As the outburst progressed, the corona cooled efficiently, the photon index steepened (Gamma >~ 2.5), and the reflection signatures, including the broad Fe K-alpha emission, were quenched, yielding a featureless, disk-dominated continuum. Concurrently, Type-C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) evolved from 0.25 Hz to 6.52 Hz. Cross-spectral timing analysis revealed that the broadband X-ray time lags changed from pronounced positive (hard) delays (~160 ms) at low frequencies to near zero as the source softened. However, a statistical analysis incorporating the measurement uncertainties shows that the broadband lags lack a significant monotonic correlation with the QPO frequency, photon index, or fractional rms. Instead, the scattered lag behavior suggests a competition between positive Comptonization delays and negative thermal reverberation. While the spectral softening and QPO acceleration provide strong evidence for a geometric contraction of the corona (whether interpreted via Lense-Thirring precession or the Two-Component Advective Flow (TCAF) paradigm), the broadband timing properties underscore the turbulent and inhomogeneous nature of the inner flow as the advancing Keplerian disk drives the source into the soft state.

papers.title: Truncation Samplers Are Nested: Comparing Decoding Rules Is a Measurement Problem
papers.abstract: Settling one comparison between two truncation samplers has cost six thousand A100-hours, and nothing says in advance how far apart two samplers can be. We observe that almost every deployed truncation rule keeps a prefix of the probability-sorted vocabulary, so any two such rules are nested at every decoding step. Nesting yields a closed-form per-step distance and a coupling under which both samplers emit identical text until they first disagree. Accumulated over a generation, this gives a separation certificate that bounds the difference between two samplers on any bounded outcome, is computable from logs a comparison already produces, and equals their sequence-level total variation distance exactly when neither rule ever overtakes the other. Two consequences follow without measurement: exactness is fragile, and certifying a small difference requires the two retained masses to agree to very high precision at every step. On six open-weight models over four math and science benchmarks, the certificate for every hyperparameter grid we tested is at least 0.998, so a bound alone rarely settles a comparison, although two members of one family can be far closer. What remains useful is the coupling, which gives an unbiased paired estimator that cuts variance $1.2$-$3.8\times$ against prompt-level pairing. Read against benchmark sizes at the default pair's variance and our point estimate of its between-prompt component, resolving a one-point difference needs 8 to 32 samples per prompt on GSM8K, MATH-500 and GPQA-Diamond and about 210 on AIME 2025; at that component's upper confidence bound GPQA-Diamond needs more than 32 and AIME 2025 cannot be resolved at any sample count. Choosing a truncation sampler is a measurement problem at least as much as a design one. The code is available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/truncation-samplers.

papers.title: Latent-Space Importance Weighting under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a transfer learning algorithm for covariate shift, integrating sample reweighting with representation learning. A key feature of our approach is the use of a lower-dimensional latent space for modeling, in contrast to conventional methods that operate directly in the high-dimensional ambient space. Our method estimates the density ratio of learned latent features for downstream weighted prediction. We establish explicit target-domain excess-risk rates with independent data folds for strictly sufficient learned representations with regular learned-space prediction scores and density ratios. We give dimension comparisons under stated smoothness conditions and a variance comparison for true weights and a fixed predictor. General finite-sample inequalities retain representation-quality errors. Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate gains from combining learned representations and latent weighting, and reveal sensitivity to initialization and domain choice.

papers.title: Look Before You Move: Agent-Interface-Aligned Supervision for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Open-world mobile manipulation requires a robot to find an object, approach it, and move it to a target receptacle from a language instruction. Training vision-language model (VLM) agents for these tasks requires demonstrations of both action selection and active vision. Existing pipelines often convert planned trajectories into high-level action labels, but shortest-path progress provides limited supervision for deciding where to look. We introduce Agent-Interface Data Alignment (AIDA), a data collection pipeline in which a teacher directly selects and executes actions through the deployed agent's skill interface. For mobile manipulation, we design teachers that maintain target visibility, recover lost targets, and approach for picking or placing. We add template-based spatial reasoning supervision and use a shared harness to organize observations, history, and outputs during training and inference. The resulting agent, AIDA-OWMM, achieves 71.76% full-task success on 170 held-out OWMM episodes. Teacher sensitivity analysis shows that active-vision demonstrations improve student success. The simulation-trained agent achieves 38% end-to-end success on a real mobile robot without additional training. Applying AIDA to a navigation subset of EmbodiedBench further demonstrates the pipeline's utility for navigation tasks.

papers.title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
papers.abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.

papers.title: The Fragility and Dynamics of LLM Pruning-Recovery Steps
papers.abstract: Structural pruning followed by a recovery stage is the standard recipe for compressing large language models (LLMs), yet the two stages are typically designed and tuned in isolation. In this work, we study how their interaction shapes the compressed model, sweeping ordering, the data that drives each stage, and the alignment of their training objectives. We find that instruction-following is the first capability to collapse under pruning, well before knowledge, reasoning, or core language modeling, and that much of the pruning in-domain loss is likely not knowledge loss but a domain-agnostic failure to respond coherently to the prompt. We find in our setting that in-domain data is the strongest pruning signal, whereas instruction-style data recovers the most. Stage order matters little, but only marginally. We further analyze how the importance ranking drifts before and after pruning. Together these results give practitioners a concrete recipe for composing pruning and recovery.

papers.title: Self-Representation Alignment in Diffusion Models for Video Background Music Generation
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have been widely used for various generative tasks. However, recent studies have demonstrated that the internal representations learned in the diffusion models' denoising process are insufficiently meaningful, which can hinder the generation performance. To address this, we propose a novel diffusion U-Net architecture enhanced by explicitly aligning the weaker representation from the earlier layer conditioned on higher noise with the better representation from the later layer conditioned on lower noise during training, which we use for the challenging multimodal task of video background music generation. Our diffusion U-Net Self-Representation Alignment (U-SRA) employs an alignment loss to effectively guide our diffusion model to learn good internal representations, thereby enabling it to produce higher-quality symbolic music conditioned on video features. We employ a cross-attention mechanism to synchronize music with video segments. Experiments on a benchmark video-music dataset demonstrate that the proposed U-SRA approach for video background music generation surpasses the state-of-the-art across key evaluation metrics, including video-music alignment and overall music quality.

papers.title: Synergistic Learning in Domain Adaptation with a Known Link: A Minimax Understanding
papers.abstract: When can combining source and target data yield much better performance than using either alone? From a minimax viewpoint, writing $R(n,n_T)$ for the minimax risk from $n$ source and $n_T$ target observations, we ask when $R(n,n_T)$ decays strictly faster than both $R(n,0)$ and $R(0,n_T)$. We call this the Synergistic Learning Phenomenon (SLP) and quantify it by the Synergistic Advantage Ratio $\mathrm{SAR}=\min(R(n,0),R(0,n_T))/R(n,n_T)$. We study domain adaptation with a known link: source regression $f$, target regression $g=\mathcal{A}f$ for a known operator $\mathcal{A}$, and possibly different designs. Three links---identity, integration, and differentiation---and the density ratio $ρ=h_T/h_S$ determine whether synergy is possible, at what rate, and in which sample-size window. For the identity link (covariate shift) with a Beta$(a,1)$ source and uniform target, a known necessary condition for SLP is $a\geq2+1/(2β)$, where $β$ is the smoothness of $f$ (Result I). An integral link $g(x)=\int_0^xf(t)\,dt$ can yield the joint rate $(nn_T)^{-1/2}$ even for a bounded ratio (Result II), and under a Beta$(a,1)$ source has a phase diagram with cuts at $a=2$ and $a=3$: integral SLP for $1<a<2$, an extra level-split rate $n_T^{-1}$ for $2<a<3$, and covariate-shift-type spatial SLP for $a>3$ (Result III). A derivative link $g=\dot f$ synergizes only under a stronger singularity (Result IV), giving a sharp integration--differentiation asymmetry under a bounded ratio. Across all three links, synergy arises from role separation: each dataset resolves a distinct bottleneck associated with the link and designs. We characterize the sample-size windows for synergy and how SAR varies with $n$ and $n_T$. Simulations support the predicted phase structure, and a mirrored integration--differentiation analysis of real vehicle and smartphone signals illustrates the asymmetry.

papers.title: SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X
papers.abstract: Cooperative driving at mixed-traffic unsignalized intersections is challenged by imperfect vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, human-driven vehicle (HV) intentions that cannot be directly communicated, and the potential incompatibility of independently generated crossing decisions. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of HV-intent prediction and CAV-intent exchange to this performance. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.

papers.title: Towards Robust Calibration Dataset for Domain-General Mixture of Experts Pruning
papers.abstract: Post-training expert pruning is a promising deployment technique for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The calibration set is an integral part of the pruning process, however, its correlation with evaluation performance is largely misunderstood and unintuitive. In this work, we present an empirical study of the robustness of calibration perturbations, specifically in MoE models. Showing how calibration size, language, and data distribution affect layer-wise expert pruning for gpt-oss-20b. Our findings reveal that (1) domain-general pruning quality receives minimal benefit from scaling calibration data beyond small sample sizes, (2) cross-lingual calibration transfers effectively, with English-only calibration maintaining strong performance across seven languages of varying typologies and scripts, and (3) a diverse calibration data resembling the pretraining distribution can yield comparable or superior performance to test-distribution data. Ultimately, we provide practical insights as a recipe for better understanding calibration for more effective domain-general expert pruning.

papers.title: Approximation Algorithms for Dual-Memory Request Scheduling in Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Disaggregated LLM inference executes the prefill and decode phases on separate resource pools, reducing interference between the two phases. However, this architecture introduces a coupled scheduling problem because a request that completes prefill retains its prompt KV cache in prefill memory until it is admitted to the decode pool. Prefill and decode admission decisions therefore jointly determine memory occupancy and request completion times. To the best of our knowledge, this problem lacks a formal formulation, and no approximation guarantees are known for request scheduling in disaggregated LLM inference. We formalize this setting as the dual-memory request scheduling (DMRS) problem, whose objective is to minimize the sum of request completion times, and prove that it is strongly NP-hard. We develop two deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithms. The first applies to instances satisfying $α<1$ and $β<1$ and achieves an approximation ratio of $8+\frac{4}{1-α}+\frac{8}{1-β}$, where $α$ and $β$ are the maximum normalized prefill and peak decode memory demands among all requests, respectively. In particular, it yields a $32$-approximation when $α,β\leq 1/2$. The second algorithm applies to all feasible instances and achieves a uniform $36$-approximation. Finally, evaluations on two H100 GPUs using trace-derived offline workloads show that the proposed algorithms reduce the sum of request completion times relative to multiple vLLM deployment baselines.

papers.title: Ellipsoids from Tangents
papers.abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for detecting and fitting multiple ellipsoids in 2D, 3D and higher-dimensional data. The representation is based on tangents to the ellipsoid together with their contact points, rather than on points alone. A tangent contributes d independent equations where a point contributes one, so each hypothesis needs fewer samples, which in turn reduces the number of iterations required to recover every ellipsoid. The problem is posed as sets of linear equations whose solutions -- the ellipsoid parameters -- are recovered robustly by clustering in parameter space. The algorithm works in all dimensions and outperforms the state of the art in 2D. The approach applies in general to the robust solution of linear equations, and so has utility beyond ellipsoid fitting.

papers.title: Coarse-Grained Predictive Resource Allocation Framework enabling In-Premise XR Collaborations
papers.abstract: Immersive extended reality (XR) applications are key enablers of human-centric connectivity in next-generation networks. However, meeting their high-throughput, ultra-low-latency, and high-reliability demands while preventing cyber-sickness remains a critical challenge, especially in environments with non-deterministic wireless connectivity. Fiber-To-The-Room (FTTR), extending widely deployed Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) infrastructure, offers a promising solution. Yet, satisfying the stringent Quality-of-Experience (QoE) requirements of XR collaborators demands robust resource allocation across the multi-tier cascade of FTTH, FTTR, and WiFi segments. In this paper, we propose a coarse-grained traffic forecasting-empowered proactive resource allocation and intelligent in-premise roaming framework. Here, artificial intelligence (AI) model complexities are scaled to the computational capabilities of each network segment. At the FTTR segment, we employ a hybrid temporal convolutional and bi-directional long short-term memory (TCN-BiLSTM) network for multi-modal XR traffic forecasting, integrating passive optical network (PON) and WiFi access points with multi-link operation (MLO) and orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA). The resulting long-horizon forecasts reduce inference frequency, enabling coordinated FTTR-WiFi resource allocation and seamless network-orchestrated mobility across rooms. At the FTTH segment, we deploy Transformer-based time-series models (e.g., Informer, Autoformer, PatchTST, and TFT) to predict the complex XR traffic aggregated in FTTR segments for transmission over the FTTH backhaul. Evaluations show Transformer-based models are up to $\sim$75% more accurate in long-horizon forecasting than the hybrid model. Extensive simulations confirm the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional methods in satisfying XR QoE requirements.

papers.title: Inverse Garment Design with Visual Agents
papers.abstract: We study the problem of inverse garment design, reconstructing simulation-ready 3D outfits with arbitrary layers from a single image, with visual agents. Unlike differentiable optimization that is time-consuming, or feed-forward methods limited by training data, we introduce DressAgent, a hierarchical agentic system that recovers garment sewing patterns through planning and closed-loop refinement grounded in physical simulation. To this end, we first present an enhanced representation based on GarmentCode for diverse styles and arbitrary dressing layers, and build the first multi-layer sewing pattern dataset with over 15K outfits for supervision and benchmarking. Inverse design then proceeds coarse to fine: In layer planning and coarse estimation, agents infer layer order and relations, peel each layer into its own view, and estimate coarse patterns. In fine-grained refinement, an agentic trio of Tailor, Critic, and Orchestrator refines patterns in a closed loop of editing, simulating, and judging against the reference with visual and measured evidence. Carefully designed tools and an evolving memory make this refinement converge on the target geometry. We also design an agentic generation method for high-fidelity textures. DressAgent outperforms feed-forward methods by a large margin, surpasses or matches differentiable optimization in a fraction of the time, and generalizes to complex layering, diverse poses, and body shapes.

papers.title: Explicit Bounds for Restricted Invertibility with Prescribed Group Cardinalities
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit lower spectral bound for independent random vectors with prescribed group multiplicities. Let $v_{ij}\in\mathbb C^d$, $1\le i\le l$, $1\le j\le k_i$, be independent random vectors with finite support and $\mathbb E v_{ij}v_{ij}^*=A_i$, where $\sum_{i=1}^l A_i=I_d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(A_i)\geε$. Set $k=\max_i k_i$, $n=\max_i\operatorname{rank}(A_i)$, and $K=\sum_{i=1}^l k_i$. If $n>(6+4\sqrt2)k$ and $2\sqrt{nk}-k<ε\le n/2$, then, with positive probability, \[ λ_K\left(\sum_{i=1}^l\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}v_{ij}v_{ij}^*\right) \ge n-(\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{n-ε})^2. \] As a consequence, we obtain a restricted invertibility result selecting exactly $k_i$ vectors from the $i$th group of a Parseval frame. The proof combines interlacing families, a reciprocal transformation of mixed characteristic polynomials, and a multivariate barrier estimate that accommodates repeated differentiation in the same variable.

papers.title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
papers.abstract: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^α$, $α>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $Γ$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.

papers.title: StreamingWAM: Streaming World Action Modeling via Chunk-Wise Staircase Flow Matching
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs), often built upon pretrained video-generation world models, have emerged as a promising framework for general-purpose and open-ended robot control. However, their real-world deployment often suffers from discontinuous and jerky execution. Existing methods typically address this issue by either improving inference efficiency or enhancing action continuity across prediction chunks, without jointly addressing both challenges. To bridge this gap, we propose StreamingWAM, a streaming-diffusion framework for WAM-based robot control. StreamingWAM combines a noise ladder for chunk-wise action prediction, a prefix rollout module for cross-chunk continuity, and dense video-history memory for temporally consistent conditioning. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic tasks demonstrate that StreamingWAM improves action continuity across static and dynamic settings, achieving competitive performance while reducing steady-state replanning latency to 72.9 ms in simulation and 57.3 ms on the real robot. The method also produces smoother action transitions, while the streaming staircase reduces sensitivity to the execution horizon K.

papers.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.

papers.title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
papers.abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(τ)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.

papers.title: Adjoint Transfer and Order-Lifting Dichotomies for 2 x 2 Matrices over Prime-Power Rings
papers.abstract: For an odd prime p, we study the change in matrix order under lifting from Z/p^k Z to Z/p^(k+1) Z. The first variation of the order defect is an affine translate of a cyclic adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p). We classify the full-order transfer for every q in GL_2(F_p): its rank is 3 for scalar elements, 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p = 3, and 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p > 3. For a Jordan element q = lambda(I + U), U^2 = 0 and U != 0, the vanishing first-order transfer for p > 3 admits an exact higher-order refinement. Writing d = (p - 1)/2, the full-order perturbation has depth d when tr(UX) != 0, depth p - 1 when tr(UX) = 0 and X is not in the span of U, and vanishes identically for X in the span of U. For p = 3, among the 27 lifts of a nonscalar order-preserving parent with determinant fixed to +1 or -1, exactly 9 preserve its order and 18 triple it; after the first increase, every further lift triples the order. We also give a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among unrestricted Jordan lifts.

papers.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations in the half-space and exterior domains
papers.abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

papers.title: The Gradient That Top-k Distillation Never Computes
papers.abstract: Many deployed distillation pipelines show the student a truncated view of the teacher: keep the top-k probabilities, renormalize, and minimize a divergence on what remains. Renormalization is assumed to account for the missing mass. We prove that it removes the visibility of tail mass, not the freedom to move it. The renormalized objective depends only on log-odds among the retained tokens, so at each position its gradient along the directions that control tail mass is exactly zero; on a real teacher that component measures $2$-$3\times10^{-15}$ of the gradient. The full-vocabulary gradient equals the truncated gradient plus a residual weighted by the tail masses, and training acts only on the first term. Without the cross-entropy term, a top-k student's tail mass drifts away from the teacher's while a full-vocabulary control moves slightly toward it; with it, the gap shrinks about fourfold but persists. On seven open-weight teachers, the retained set determines the teacher's distribution only from $k=d+1$ ($d$ the hidden dimension): recovery is exact from there on all seven, and commonly cached sizes sit below it. In our off-policy runs the practical effect is real but smaller than the choice of teacher-student pair. Renormalization is a normalization, not a safeguard. The code is available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/top-k-distillation.

papers.title: An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.

papers.title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
papers.abstract: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

papers.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
papers.abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.

papers.title: Topological extensions of elementary measurable spaces
papers.abstract: An elementary space is a pair $(X, \mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A$ is an algebra of subsets of $X$. Every elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$ is naturally a topological space when equipped with the topology $τ_{\mathcal A}$ generated by $\mathcal A$. Elementary mappings on elementary spaces are defined in a manner analogous to measurable mappings on measurable spaces. In addition, the notion of an {\it extension} of an elementary space is introduced. Let $M(X, \mathcal A)$, denote the ring of all real-valued elementary functions on $(X, \mathcal A)$. In this article, we study the ring $M(X, \mathcal A)$ and extensions of an elementary space. We show that, for any elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$, there exists a unique compact elementary extension $(β_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A})$ of $X$, analogous to the Stone-$\check C$ech compactification, which contains every other extension of $X$. This extension has the property that every elementary map from $X$ into any compact topological space extends continuously to $β_{\mathcal A}X$. Next, we show that $β_{\mathcal A}X$ contains a realcompact extension $(\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A}_R)$ of $X$, such that every elementary map from $X$ into any realcompact topological space extends continuously to $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Moreover, $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$ is the smallest realcompact extension of $X$ and $(X, \mathcal A)$ is realcompact if and only if $X=\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Also, we see that, every metric space equipped with the $σ$-algebra of all Borel sets is realcompact. Finally, we observe that the maximal ring of quotients of $M(X, \mathcal A)$ is the direct limit of locally constant (continuous) functions on dense open subsets of $(X, τ_{\mathcal A})$. Some questions raised in the literature are also answered.

papers.title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
papers.abstract: We establish global well-posedness and sharp higher-order decay estimates for the fractional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in $\R^{3}$ with fractional Lamé--Navier dissipation $\Lame^αu$ with $α\in[1/2,1]$, and Riesz coupling $Λ^{2β}φ=ρ-\barρ$ with $β\in[0,1]$, where $Λ:=(-Δ)^{1/2}$ and $\barρ>0$ denotes the constant background density. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium in $H^{Nα}$ with $N\geq3$ and $Nα>5/2$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions. Furthermore, we propagate the negative Sobolev norms with uniform-in-time bounds and derive the higher-order decay estimates, provided that the initial perturbation additionally belongs to $\dot{H}^{-\vartheta}$ for some $\vartheta\in[0,3/2)$. Moreover, we establish the optimality of these decay rates within the prescribed initial data class for the velocity and the Riesz potential in their natural energy norms. The density decay exponents are also optimal whenever the available regularity permits the full Riesz-induced gain. The analysis relies on a nonlinear energy structure adapted to both fractional dissipation and Riesz interaction, together with Sobolev interpolation. The optimality of the decay is proved by constructing smooth initial data localized at low frequencies and proving matching upper and lower decay bounds for the resulting solutions. These solutions show that the low-frequency linear dynamics including the Riesz-induced density gain, persists under nonlinear evolution.

papers.title: FireNav: Decision-Oriented Reconstruction Evidence Routing for Vision-Language Navigation in Indoor Fire Environments
papers.abstract: In real-world indoor fire environments, visual degradation severely impairs instruction grounding, waypoint prediction, and long-horizon exploration in vision-language navigation (VLN). Although image restoration offers a natural means to mitigate such visual degradation, existing methods primarily optimize reconstruction fidelity, which does not necessarily translate into better navigation decisions and may even corrupt task-critical cues when applied indiscriminately. In this paper, we present FireNav, a decision-oriented reconstruction evidence routing framework that aligns visual restoration with navigation utility in VLN. To advance this task, we first contribute FireVLN-Bench, a paired indoor fire navigation benchmark with clean references preserving task semantics, safety supervision, and matched settings for continuous navigation and robot execution with simulated dynamics. Our FireNav retains native visual tokens and treats latent reconstruction features as auxiliary evidence, where a lightweight router leverages visual features, task context, and prior execution states to determine whether such evidence should be admitted and how strongly it should contribute to the visual tokens. To learn when reconstruction is beneficial, we further introduce decision utility calibration, which compares action prediction losses with and without candidate evidence under the same state, thereby supervising evidence selection according to its contribution to waypoint, heading, and arrival prediction. Experiments demonstrate that FireNav consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both navigation success and path efficiency across evaluation settings.

papers.title: Almost Lossless Transfer for Cuttable Distributed Problems
papers.abstract: We study constant-round LOCAL approximation for additive local vertex-subset minimization problems. Given a $k$-uniform $α$-approximation on a hereditary source class closed under disjoint union, Bonamy, Das, Gavoille, Picavet, Suomela, and Wesolek obtained ratio $α(d+1)+1$ on locally nice target classes of asymptotic dimension $d$. We prove two transfers with ratios $α+1+η$ and $α+η$ for every $η>0$. These bounds require the stronger local niceness assumption at a larger scale that depends on $η$. The first algorithm keeps their repair construction and increases the radius used to detect errors. We average over partitions of the graph to bound the retained cost without the factor $d+1$. These partitions are used only in the analysis. The second algorithm tests several deletion widths around the errors. In each component of the repair zone, it chooses a smallest union of retained choices and an exact repair. Averaging over the widths bounds the cost counted twice and yields ratio $α+η$. Both transfers are deterministic and computable, use arbitrary distinct numerical identifiers, and need no knowledge of the graph size. Their outputs also satisfy local uniformity guarantees. For 2-domination on graphs of bounded Euler genus, the same planar source gives ratio $19$ through the earlier transfer and $6+η$ through ours. For minimum dominating set, our transfer gives ratio $7+\varepsilon$ on graphs formed by attaching a clique of arbitrary size at one vertex of a planar graph, using the source algorithm of Amiri and Siebertz. This class satisfies our target assumptions and allows nonempty error sets. Its Euler genus is unbounded, so their guarantee for graphs of bounded Euler genus does not cover the whole class.

papers.title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence and Topological Degree
papers.abstract: This paper is a continuation of Part~I \cite{QTWPartI}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the CR Nirenberg problem were established. We prove some existence and degree results for the CR Nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. More precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. Without symmetry, we derive a Leray--Schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. We also obtain Aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.

papers.title: Inferred and Residual Parameter Interactions in Syntax Dynamics
papers.abstract: What makes natural languages diversify, in their syntactic structure, even when sharing a largely common origin? We refine our simple model, which focuses on the glassy dynamics induced by a network of interactions between syntactic parameters. Distinguishing between symmetric interaction weights that can be inferred from the observed statistics of syntax across many languages, and additional asymmetric weights assigned at random, we show that both components are needed, with similar overall strength, to account for plausible long-term syntactic dynamics. An approximate balance can combine the glassy metastability provided by the inferred weights with the chaotic diversification induced by the residual asymmetric weights.

papers.title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior. These constructions show that smoothness of the complete contour does not force contour--boundary equality and that internal critical-value branches persist under monomial transformations, controlled perturbations, and finite monomial coverings.21 pages, 14 figures

papers.title: Side-Vent Design for Microphone-Based Mechanomyography Sensors: Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of Contact Dependence
papers.abstract: Wearable muscle sensing for rehabilitation, assistive robotics, and electrical-stimulation feedback needs mechanomyography sensors less sensitive to fit changes during wear. In microphone-based mechanomyography, cavity pressure depends on rim contact, a dependence housing design has rarely targeted. This study evaluates a side-vented housing, whose vent opens a pressure-relief path in parallel with the rim to lower contact dependence, and quantifies the acoustic-gain cost. Thermoviscous finite-element simulations compared twenty cavity configurations under prescribed source motion. Paired bench sweeps over 10-200 Hz on both housings compared direct contact with a Gap-ring spacer, a radially grooved spacer ring. At 100 Hz, side venting reduced the simulated acoustic-gain variation across 0.10-0.50 mm rim clearances from 25.8 to 10.0 dB and cost 5.5 dB of gain at 0.20 mm clearance. Velocity fields and branch-flow calculations identified this path. At the higher speaker drive level, the Gap-ring spacer caused median attenuations of 13.6 dB (vented) and 30.1 dB (unvented) relative to direct contact. In this front end, a 35.9-dB signal-gain increase at 100 Hz raised the calculated operational-amplifier voltage-noise gain by 1.6 dB. A single-participant demonstration of paced elbow flexion and extension compared envelope timing and spectra between housings, finding similar envelope timing (correlation 0.935) and broadly similar spectra (correlation 0.956). Vent area trades acoustic gain against contact dependence and can therefore serve as a housing design parameter.

papers.title: A Quantum Analogue of the Covering Lemma: Limits of Exact Anonymous Computation
papers.abstract: Can quantum communication determine the size of an anonymous network when no size bound is known? Classical impossibility proofs rely on the covering lemma: an execution can be reproduced on a larger network with the same local structure. Quantum interference invalidates this argument - a measurement record possible on a network can become impossible on a cover. We show that the impossibility of exact counting nevertheless survives. Our main result is a quantum analogue of the covering lemma that preserves local possibilities rather than complete executions. Within a cyclic covering family, every local measurement outcome possible at a node remains possible at a corresponding node in every sufficiently large network. This holds even after information has travelled around the smaller network, beyond the reach of a simple locality argument. We extend the principle to the universal covering tree and finite covers with sufficiently long cycles. The proof combines tensor-network methods with graph coverings: a common representation across network sizes turns normalization into a constraint on which local outcomes can occur. For uniform synchronous protocols with independently prepared nodes, this support-lifting principle rules out zero-error counting and even the production of a guaranteed finite size bound on anonymous rings and the other cyclic covering families considered here. It also rules out exact leader election with termination in finite time with probability one on these families. Measurements, classical control, and local memory growing with time are allowed; no predetermined running-time bound is assumed. Quantum interference thus defeats execution lifting without enabling infallible certification of network size.

papers.title: Realistic Simulation of Valence-band Photoemission Spectra by using First-principles Calculations on the Basis of FLAPW Method
papers.abstract: In order to reproduce experimental photoemission spectroscopy (PES) data by using band structure calculations with linearized augmented-plane-wave method, we developed a new method to calculate the atomic-subshell photoelectron differential cross section (PE-DCS) of the valence band. PE-DCS was calculated to be the sum of the products of the partial density of states (PDOS) and the photoionization differential cross section (PI-DCS) of each atomic subshell. To construct an appropriate PDOS beyond the conventional muffin-tin sphere (MTS) PDOS, we proposed a ``nearly-neutral atomic sphere", which can be defined as a natural extension of MTS. Although the calculational method for atomic-subshell PI-DCS was the standard Hartree-Fock-Slater method, we developed a new computer code in order to deal with the unoccupied electron shells in the ground state of isolated atoms up to $\sim$10 keV. Details of the PE-DCS calculations were examined by using two simple examples of Na metal and NaCl, and then, the method was applied to hard x-ray PES (HX-PES) data of CuAlO$_2$. The experimental spectra were satisfactorily reproduced, demonstrating the potential applications of our method to HX-PES spectra of many compounds.

papers.title: CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning
papers.abstract: Materials synthesis planning (MSP) connects AI-driven materials discovery to experimental realization by proposing precursors, synthesis operations, and processing conditions for a target material. Existing approaches predict these components separately or in pairs and treat conditions only as a prediction target. Consequently, MSP remains centered on recipe prediction: it leaves unexplored how conditions can serve as process context for constructing synthesis routes, and it does not address which candidate routes should be executed under limited experimental resources. We propose CondMSP, which extends MSP from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning. CondMSP predicts temperature, time, and atmosphere by combining a joint predictor with variable-specific experts, and then uses these predictions both as process context, grounding the generation and retrieval of operation sequences, and as execution requirements, specifying which thermal stages can share a furnace run and at what cost. This specification is held fixed across all compared methods; within it, CondMSP ranks routes across precursor sets by a common utility and, under furnace budgets, jointly selects routes and allocates their thermal stages by constrained optimization. CondMSP improves condition and operation prediction and, under this shared constraint, raises reference-recipe recovery from 27.9% to 32.9% at three simulated furnace runs per target and from 34.7% to 40.0% at 30 trials, while a new evaluation set of 2,344 targets supports generalization beyond oxide-dominated training chemistry.

papers.title: Squeeze-Aware-YOLO: Early Channel Recalibration and Multi-Scale Fusion for Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection
papers.abstract: Traffic sign detection plays a vital role in intelligent transportation systems, supporting the safe operation of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles. Despite significant progress in real-time object detection, accurately identifying traffic signs under challenging conditions remains difficult. Variations in lighting, adverse weather, motion blur, and partial occlusion often reduce detection performance, especially for small or visually degraded signs where important spatial information can be lost. To address these challenges, we propose Squeeze-Aware-YOLO, a lightweight traffic sign detection framework that introduces a multi-branch bottleneck module combining convolutional kernels of different sizes with a Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanism to improve feature extraction and adaptive channel weighting. In addition, we integrate the Multi-Branch Auxiliary Feature Pyramid Network and Re-parameterized Heterogeneous Multi-Scale modules to strengthen multi-scale feature representation and feature fusion while preserving real-time inference efficiency for practical deployment. The proposed approach is evaluated on the Bangladeshi Traffic Sign Detection Dataset, the CSUST Chinese Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark 2021, and the German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark, achieving mAP@0.5 scores of 74.7%, 79.4%, and 84.0%, respectively, while consistently outperforming recent state-of-the-art YOLO-based traffic sign detectors. These findings demonstrate that combining multi-scale receptive fields, channel attention, and enhanced feature fusion enables more accurate and robust traffic sign detection while maintaining the computational efficiency required for real-world deployment.

papers.title: A Co-Located MMG-FES Wearable Interface for Action-Updated State-Gated Stimulation
papers.abstract: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) assists movement, but fixed schedules cannot track how a repeatedly activated muscle changes, and surface electromyography (EMG) near the stimulation electrodes is often obscured by artifacts. Prior work recorded mechanomyography (MMG) passively during closed-loop FES cycling and estimated FES-induced fatigue or predicted fatigue for FES control, without gating stimulation with stimulated-site MMG. In this study, we present VG-FES, a wearable module co-locating microphone-based MMG, programmable charge-balanced biphasic stimulation, and embedded state-gated control at one on-skin thigh site. After each action, we compare rectus femoris (RF) mean power frequency (MPF) with an early-session baseline of the same direction, giving a relative state. A threshold on its window means enables fixed-duration bursts separated by rest periods. During onboard stimulation, MMG remained recordable, whereas near-site EMG was artifact-dominated. Under prolonged external stimulation, cycle-wise MMG tracked an independent local-pressure reference (Spearman rho = 0.968). In leave-one-session-out evaluation on 2284 squat actions (11 sessions, eight participants), MMG-based action segmentation reached an event-detection F1 of 0.923 and direction classification a balanced accuracy of 0.925. Online, over 15.69 min of self-paced squats, one participant received four bursts while MMG acquisition and action monitoring continued. Mechanical feedback from the stimulated site offers wearable FES and assistive robotics a per-action basis for state-gated stimulation.

papers.title: Tornado Wave-Encoded Point Spread Functions for Multi-Period Three-Dimensional Localization Imaging
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) localization microscopy using rotational point spread functions (PSFs) is fundamentally challenged by limited axial range, poor PSF compactness, and depth-decoding ambiguity -- particularly in dense specimens with heavy PSF overlap. To address these limitations, we introduce a 3D localization approach based on tornado wave (ToW)-PSFs, combined with a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to decode continuous rotational patterns and resolve multi-period axial ambiguity. Our engineered PSF encodes the 3D position of each nanoparticle into a compact double-lobe pattern whose orientation rotates with axial position. This design yields a clean, well-defined structural evolution across an unprecedented 15 um axial range, with an average rotation rate of 21.8 degrees/um, ensuring robust long-range depth encoding. To recover coordinates from overlapping emitters, we systematically benchmark a conventional matching-pursuit (MP) algorithm against our CNN. While MP performs adequately in sparse scenes, the CNN demonstrates exceptional robustness in dense fields, achieving a 70.24% localization accuracy at 20 particles per image-substantially outperforming MP's 22.52% -- while also significantly suppressing axial period-jump errors. Experimental validation on nanoparticles confirms reliable single- and multi-particle localization throughout the entire working range. Our results establish ToW-PSFs as a powerful and practical optical encoding strategy for high-density, extended-range 3D localization imaging.

papers.title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction. Exact triangular and trapezoidal families are complemented by positive-genus investigations exhibiting bounded amoeba-complement components. These results show that a perfectly exposed amoeba contour does not determine the real structure, logarithmic sheet number, or Harnack type of the underlying curve.

papers.title: Single-Particle Spectroscopy and Cross-Barrier Dynamics in Inhomogeneous Luttinger Liquids via Unified Field Bosonization Technique
papers.abstract: The Unified Field Bosonization Technique (UFBT) is employed to investigate the single-particle properties of inhomogeneous Luttinger liquids containing localized clusters of impurities in the presence of forward-scattering interactions. Within this framework, fermionic two-point correlation functions are used to derive the leading-order singular contributions to the dynamical density of states (DDOS) and the cross-barrier tunneling conductance. The results reveal distinct power-law behaviours of the DDOS near the impurity cluster and in the far-field regime. The tunneling conductance exhibits a power-law temperature dependence, decreasing with decreasing temperature for repulsive interactions and increasing for attractive interactions, while remaining temperature-independent in the noninteracting limit. The impurity cluster modifies the amplitudes and spatial structure of these observables, whereas their characteristic power-law exponents are determined solely by the interaction parameters. The formulation accommodates arbitrary impurity strengths without requiring perturbative expansions in the impurity or interaction strengths. The characteristic scaling behaviour emerges directly from the fermionic correlation functions, without an explicit renormalization-group (RG) treatment of the impurity strength, while the weak-interaction limit recovers the leading perturbative correction to the tunneling response. These findings establish UFBT as a unified framework for describing local spectral properties and cross-barrier transport in inhomogeneous Luttinger liquids.

papers.title: Proposal for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions
papers.abstract: Scaling trapped-ion optical clocks to hundreds of ions remains a major challenge due to inhomogeneous frequency shifts in large ion crystals. Here, we propose a circular surface-trap architecture for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions. The rotational symmetry of the ion crystal suppresses the main sources of inhomogeneity, quadrupole shift.We investigate the feasibility of a clock based on a ring crystal of 400 $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ ions and propose a suitable experimental setup configuration. We have shown that circular configuration of ions leads to suppression by two orders of magnitude of the quadrupole shift comparing to the linear trap. Combined with stray-field compensation and dynamical decoupling techniques, this architecture provides a pathway toward multi-ion optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainty at the $10^{-18}$ level and an expected 20-fold improvement in frequency stability compared to single ion clocks.

papers.title: Diagonal recovery from noisy Fourier--Hermite coefficients: exact orders of the error
papers.abstract: We consider the recovery of functions of the weighted Wiener classes $W_s^μ$ from perturbed Fourier--Hermite coefficients in the metric of $L_\infty(\mathbb R)$. For the summation methods of the class $\mathcal S^θ$ we find error estimates on $W_s^μ$. The estimates take into account the behaviour of the Hermite functions both in the oscillatory region and near the turning point: the maxima of functions with different indices are attained at different points, and the supremum of a sum over a block of indices is substantially smaller than the sum of the suprema. Owing to this, in particular, we establish a common lower bound for all finite diagonal methods; for $s\ne4/3$ and $p\ne4/3$ it matches the upper bound and gives the exact order of the error in this class, while at the critical points the gap between the bounds does not exceed $(\log(e/δ))^{1/4}$ up to a constant. If, in addition, $s>4/3$ or $p<4/3$, then this order is also optimal among all recovery operators that use the whole sequence of data.

papers.title: Physical Layer Security for Movable Antenna-Aided Mixed-Field ISAC
papers.abstract: Movable antenna (MA) can enhance the physical layer security (PLS) performance of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, most existing works assume either near-field (NF) or far-field (FF) propagation models for both communication users (CUs) and targets. This paper considers a more practical scenario where multiple CUs, an eavesdropper (Eve), and multiple targets are in a mixed near- and far-field environment due to the changes in the propagation field caused by antenna position updates in MA with a unified array response and continuous NF/FF weights. To evaluate the PLS performance of MA-aided ISAC in mixed-field environments, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the sum secrecy rate (SSR) of CUs by jointly designing the transmit beamforming and antenna positions at the transmitter. The problem is highly non-convex, so a two-layer algorithm is proposed to iteratively solve the problem using the projected gradient ascent (PGA) method and the Lagrangian dual transform. Since the abrupt switch between the NF and the FF models during antenna movement can cause the objective function to oscillate during iteration, the unified array response is combined with the Barzilai-Borwein step, Armijo line search, and precise projection to ensure that the SSR does not decrease during the iteration and the objective function is differentiable on the Rayleigh boundary. Numerical results show that the MA-ISAC using the mixed-field model achieves almost identical PLS performance to that of using the full NF model in terms of SSR, and both outperform the FF model. Using the mismatched FF model during antenna position updates results in a loss of MA gain, potentially making MA inferior to the FA-based system using the correct model.

papers.title: Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision
papers.abstract: Accurate lesion segmentation in mammography is important for computer-aided breast cancer diagnosis, but dense pixel-level annotations remain costly and limited. Existing public segmentation datasets usually cover only a small set of lesion types with manually delineated masks, whereas larger mammography datasets often provide only image-level diagnostic labels. This annotation mismatch makes it difficult to train segmentation models that can generalize to rare or weakly annotated lesion categories. To address this problem, we study open-vocabulary mammographic lesion segmentation under a mixed-supervision setting, where pixel-level masks are available for base lesion categories and image-level labels are available for a broader set of categories. We propose a two-branch framework that jointly learns from segmentation data and classification data. The segmentation branch learns lesion boundaries from annotated masks, while the classification branch introduces additional image-level semantic supervision. To better transfer image-level supervision to lesion-relevant regions, we further introduce a Lesion-wise Attentive Classifier that maintains category-specific feature prototypes and generates lesion-aware attention maps for foreground feature pooling. This design reduces the influence of background tissue and encourages more compact lesion representations. Experiments on multiple mammography datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation baselines on both base and novel lesion categories, while reducing the gap to fully supervised models that require dense target-domain masks. Qualitative results further indicate that our method produces more complete lesion localization for small, low-contrast, and visually subtle mammographic findings.

papers.title: Joint Contrastive-Adversarial Representation Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
papers.abstract: Effective unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) requires a representation that captures transferable structure from both the labeled source domain and the unlabeled target domain. We introduce Joint Contrastive-Adversarial Representation Learning (JCAR), a two-stage framework that learns a common representation from the union of unlabeled source and target samples by combining contrastive learning with adversarial domain alignment, and then freezes the representation to fit a source-supervised predictor. We establish a non-asymptotic excess-risk bound for this procedure that couples representation and domain-discriminator estimation while separating downstream prediction, with explicit neural-network approximation errors. Under the stated assumptions and common Hölder smoothness $β\geq1$, the bound identifies a sufficiently large unlabeled-sample regime in which the downstream rate is $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(m^{-β/(2β+d)})$, where $m$ counts labeled source samples and logarithmic factors are suppressed. The labeled-sample exponent is governed by the latent dimension $d$ rather than the ambient dimension $p$, which enters the pretraining cost. Experiments on Office-31, Office-Home, and DomainNet demonstrate clear transfer gains across diverse domain shifts, with particularly strong performance when representations are learned from scratch.

papers.title: ProML: Progressive Multi-label Learning
papers.abstract: Multi-label learning typically pursues model construction through the joint optimization of label fitting, correlation modeling, and structural regularization. While empirically effective, such a coupled paradigm imposes multiple learning objectives on a single predictive parameter matrix, forcing it to simultaneously fit observed labels and encode structural priors. This coupling may induce ill-conditioned optimization geometry, increase hyper-parameter sensitivity, and complicate capacity control. To address the these issues, this paper proposes a Progressive Multi-Label Learning (ProML) framework, which decouples direct label fitting from predictor learning via the introduction of an auxiliary predictive variable. This auxiliary variable admits a closed-form solution, yielding an equivalent profiled objective in which the supervised fitting term is scaled by a trade-off parameter. This result provides a unified view of ProML and conventional coupled learning, with the latter recovered as a limiting case. We theoretically analyze the optimization geometry of ProML and show that, under quadratic positive semidefinite structural regularization, ProML attenuates the dominant curvature of the fitting term, enlarges the stable learning rate range, and provides a controllable fidelity-regularization trade-off. Further, we instantiate the ProML for multi-label feature selection task by integrating global-local label priors and row-sparse regularization. Extensive experiments and controlled optimization analyses on 12 benchmark datasets empirically corroborate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the robust and competitive performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
papers.abstract: Computational research requires repeated decisions about models, calculations and the interpretation of results. We introduce Brilliance, an agent that combines large language models, reusable physics expertise and numerical simulation to construct and revise investigations in accelerator physics. Starting from a detailed expert-specified request, Brilliance develops an ideal storage-ring lattice meeting the specified emittance ceiling and sampled nonlinear-acceptance criteria after revising optics that fail particle-tracking tests. Further scientist-guided exploration produces a candidate with a natural emittance of 6.51 pm rad and millimeter-scale transverse acceptance, while exposing unresolved momentum-acceptance limitations. Using measured responses from the High Energy Photon Source, Brilliance also performs offline optics calibration consistent with an independent specialist analysis. An expert-module ablation examines how reusable domain knowledge influences research choices and outcomes. Here, we demonstrate a practical route to scientist-agent collaboration in sustained numerical research.

papers.title: Generalizable fetal brain biometry via adaptive artificial intelligence
papers.abstract: Reliable fetal brain biometry on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosing congenital brain anomalies, but artificial intelligence models often lose accuracy under domain shifts. We developed BioTTA, a backbone-agnostic, source-free unsupervised test-time adaptation framework that adapts pretrained models online to individual unlabeled target volumes. This retrospective multicohort study included 394 reconstructed 3D fetal brain MRI volumes at 20-39 gestational weeks, with 11 biometric measurements annotated by radiologists. BioTTA was developed on single-center turbo spin-echo MRI and evaluated on three datasets representing cross-sequence, cross-center, and cross-nation shifts. Biometry accuracy was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and the percentage of correct measurements within 4 mm. A web-based reporting platform mapped measurements onto normative growth trajectories and was evaluated against radiologists in four multicenter disease cohorts covering germinal matrix-intraventricular hemorrhage, ventriculomegaly, and cerebellar abnormality. Across all three target datasets, BioTTA outperformed auto-SVRTK, source-only models, and FetalSynthGen, while matching models finetuned with target labels. MAEs ranged from 1.10 to 1.46 mm with a convolutional backbone and from 1.46 to 2.25 mm with a transformer backbone. Diagnostic accuracy ranged from 82.1% to 95.0%, comparable to a senior radiologist. BioTTA supports accurate, generalizable fetal brain biometry and standardized prenatal brain growth assessment across heterogeneous MRI sources.

papers.title: Generative AI enables human-centered design of sustainable plant-based foods
papers.abstract: Dietary transitions away from animal-based meat could reduce food-related environmental burdens, but plant-based alternatives must compete on flavor, texture, and overall liking. Here we extend a generative AI framework with 469 plant-based burger recipes and use it to create six formulations across five primary ingredients: bean, chickpea, lentil, mushroom, and oat. An executive chef translates the AI-generated formulations into standardized preparation protocols and refines the ingredient quantities based on culinary expertise. The integration of generative modeling and culinary expertise defines a human-centered generative AI framework for food design. We evaluate the six burgers in a blinded sensory survey with 101 participants in an operating restaurant and quantify their land use, greenhouse gas emissions, eutrophication potential, and scarcity-weighted water use. We use Big Mac scores from a previous survey as an iconic commercial benchmark. The mushroom burger achieves mean flavor, texture, and overall liking scores similar to the Big Mac, with less than one-third of its estimated environmental impact. The other formulations reduce the estimated impact further, in several cases to near one-tenth of the Big Mac value, but receive lower liking scores. Mixed-effects models quantify associations between sensory attributes and human liking and retain predictive accuracy on independent survey data, with mean absolute errors no greater than 0.52 points on a seven-point scale. Together, these results demonstrate how generative design, culinary expertise, human sensory response, and environmental assessment can converge to create sustainable foods that people want to eat.

papers.title: Screening Collapse under Recursive Synthetic Data
papers.abstract: Recursive synthetic-data training can degrade a fitted model, but its effects on the variable-screening stage that precedes model fitting are less understood. When each generation labels data for the next, a marginal screener ranks variables against the current pseudo-label target rather than the original response. Across generations, this target drift can erode or reverse the active--inactive score margin and cause screening to discard variables that clean-label screening would retain. We call this process \emph{screening collapse}. In a Gaussian linear model with minimum-norm recursive generators, we establish finite-sample screening bounds, characterize a late-generation information-loss limit, and derive a minimax impossibility result. Screening collapse can precede and compound ordinary model collapse: omitted variables incur a covariance-weighted loss that no refit restricted to the selected variables can eliminate, while recursive labels further degrade estimation on the retained variables. We also examine two approaches to mitigating screening collapse. Fixed-fraction real-label retention preserves a clean-label component but leaves resolution fixed, whereas data accumulation can avoid screening collapse if the pooled target preserves a positive margin and the growing sample resolves it. Numerical experiments on gene-expression data support the theoretical findings.

papers.title: From Dirac Neutrino Mass to Dark Radiation: An $A_4$-Symmetric FIMP Dark Matter Framework
papers.abstract: We propose a unified $A_4\times Z_2\times U(1)_L$ framework for generating small Dirac neutrino masses and address dark matter through feeble interactions in an extended particle physics model. The model extends the Standard Model with a pair of heavy vector-like neutral $A_4$ fermions $N(N_{L,R})$, two additional flavon fields $η$ and $φ$, among which $η$ being a $Z_2$-odd inert scalar and a dark-sector vector-like fermion field $χ$. We numerically explore the Dirac-sector Yukawa couplings and identify the parameter region that is consistent with the {\tt NuFit 6.1} neutrino oscillation data at the $3σ$ level. The dark matter candidate $χ$, stabilized by the $Z_2$ symmetry, is produced non-thermally through the decay $N_L\rightarrowχ+η$. By solving the Boltzmann equation, we find that the observed relic abundance, $Ω_{\rm DM}h^2\simeq0.12$, can be reproduced for freeze-in couplings of order $λ\sim10^{-5.5}$--$10^{-7.5}$ over the considered dark matter mass range. For the chosen parameter space, we also verify the interaction rate remains below the Hubble expansion rate, confirming $χ$ never reaches thermal equilibrium. Thus, our results demonstrate that the model provides a consistent realization of Dirac neutrino masses and FIMP dark matter within a common symmetry-based setup. The presence of light Dirac RH neutrinos can contribute to the dark radiation and hence the effective degrees of freedom via thermal and non-thermal processes. We further estimate the contribution of the light right-handed neutrinos to \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\), finding a maximum characteristic value of \(ΔN_{\rm eff}\simeq0.14\) in the benchmark parameter region.

papers.title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.

papers.title: From Stages to States: Unified Iterative Reasoning for MLLMs
papers.abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) substantially enhances the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by explicitly modeling intermediate reasoning processes. However, most learning-based MCoT methods follow a stage-centric paradigm, where different reasoning behaviors are assigned to predefined stages and optimized separately.
