For a broad class of response functions, we show that observational feature-discovery evidence generally does not identify this attribution, and derive an exact gradient-based decomposition of the gap between linear-probe predictions and intervention attribution. Across four model-SAE pairs, median probe-to-attribution magnitude ratios range from tens to hundreds, while attributions closely track small-step steering. For single-latent ablations with nonzero effects, gradient predictions match the realized sign in 91-97% of cases, compared with 17-35% for probe-implied changes. Attribution-selected sets also produce larger absolute mean ablation effects on held-out prompts than sets selected by correlation, rank tests or probe coefficients. Together, these results establish intervention attribution as a principled, gradient-estimable target for selecting SAE features for intervention.

papers.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le α<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,α}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+α}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $α=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
papers.abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{dα} V(N^α\cdot),\, α>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.

papers.title: Jensen-Bregman split Gibbs sampling
papers.abstract: Split Gibbs sampling (SGS) is a versatile tool to sample from complex posterior distributions, such as those arising in imaging inverse problems. However, existing SGS instances are limited to quadratic variable couplings, restricting their applicability to Gaussian likelihoods. This letter genearalizes SGS to non-Euclidean geometry by introducing a coupling kernel defined through a Jensen-Bregman divergence. This framework not only enables posterior sampling in these settings but also unifies several \emph{ad hoc} sampling schemes from the literature under a principled theoretical foundation.

papers.title: Sharper Frames, Worse Rooms: Viewpoint Coverage Dominates Image Quality in Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Grounded spatial reasoning about indoor scenes rests on a geometric reconstruction that the multimodal system does not itself produce. Feed-forward multi-view reconstruction models operate under a fixed view budget, making frame selection a critical upstream decision. We show that under this setting the conventional preference for sharp frames can be actively harmful. Across nine handheld room scans, selecting the sharpest 16 of 200 candidate frames is the worst strategy we test, reaching 48\% room dimension error where uniform temporal sampling reaches 3\%. We trace this failure to a coupling between image quality and camera motion: sharp frames tend to occur during slow motion and therefore concentrate the selection in a narrow angular region, leaving $192^\circ$ of the room unobserved in the case we illustrate and over $300^\circ$ in the worst cells. A $2\times2$ factorial experiment that independently manipulates viewpoint spread and per-frame sharpness shows that spread has roughly three times the main effect of quality, and that blurry but well spread selections outperform sharp but clustered selections in 8 of 9 captures. The advantage also diminishes as the frame budget increases and angular coverage saturates, consistent with this mechanism. Finally, we ask whether the failure is detectable at inference: the reconstruction model's multi-view consistency score increases with reconstruction error, while a vision-language model given the same frames reports confidence unrelated to its own spatial estimation error. Under small view budgets, viewpoint coverage is a more important constraint than per-frame image quality, and neither uncertainty signal available at inference reveals this upstream failure.

papers.title: Attention Sinks in VLMs Are Borrowed, Not Seen
papers.abstract: We study how to detect and mitigate visual attention sinks in vision-language models (VLMs). Visual attention sinks are image tokens that absorb a large share of attention over the image regardless of the query or task, and they mislead methods that treat attention maps as a record of where the model ``looked.'' Prior work has detected sinks through massive activation dimensions and proposed redistributing their attention, but none have addressed what makes a token become a sink. Comparing six candidate detectors on ten VLMs from four families, we find that only the centered cosine similarity between an image token's key and the key of the language model's text-sink detects visual sinks. Thus, a visual sink is an image token whose key aligns with the text-sink's key. Moving a sink's key component along this direction to the median of the image keys sends its attention back to the text-sink (\textbf{Are Borrowed}) while leaving model answers unchanged~(\textbf{Not Seen}). Building on this, we propose a training-free, entropy-triggered re-look that first cleans the attention map, then crops the most-attended region of the cleaned map and inserts it into the reasoning trace. Cleaning adds negligible computation to the forward pass, and the re-look improves accuracy with a mean gain of $+4.3$ points on fine-detail VQA benchmarks across model families.

papers.title: GuidanceNFT: NFT-Based Reward Fine-Tuning of Guided Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: DiffusionNFT (NFT) fine-tunes diffusion models toward task-specific rewards, but optimizing these rewards does not guarantee fidelity to the full prompt. Although classifier-free guidance (CFG) strengthens prompt alignment, NFT is formulated as a CFG-free method, and applying CFG to the fine-tuned velocity field can reduce the optimized reward. This motivates optimizing rewards over the guided output distribution while seeking to retain its prompt alignment. However, applying standard NFT directly to guided samples can cause reward degradation or training collapse. We trace this failure to a mismatch between the reference velocity used in the NFT loss and the score of the guided sample distribution, which biases the improvement direction. We propose GuidanceNFT, which estimates the matching reference velocity through online flow matching on guided samples and uses it to correct both regression terms. With an exact reference, the corrected objective recovers NFT's intended update. In our experiments, the learned correction sustains reward improvement under both explicit and built-in guidance. On SD3.5-M, GuidanceNFT achieves higher optimized rewards than NFT with and without CFG across GenEval, text-rendering, and multi-reward objectives, together with better overall prompt alignment as measured by off-domain evaluation metrics. Experiments on models with built-in guidance, including Model Guidance and ELF, further demonstrate improved ImageNet generation, a better perplexity-entropy tradeoff on OpenWebText, and higher accuracy on GSM8K.

papers.title: Low-Latency Belief-Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes with Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling
papers.abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) decoding because of its low complexity and low latency, but short cycles and degeneracy can limit its error-correction performance. Reinforcement-learned sequential scheduling (RL-S) substantially improves this performance by adapting the variable node (VN) update order, although Q-table storage and heap-based selection introduce additional overhead. We propose bucket RL-S (B-RL-S), which quantizes learned Q-values into integer priorities and schedules VN updates using dynamically maintained first-in, first-out buckets. Without retraining or changing the BP message updates, B-RL-S reduces policy storage and refreshes only priorities affected by local residual syndrome changes. A fixed number of priority levels enables constant-time VN selection and queue relocation. For the $[[288,12,18]]$ bivariate bicycle code over the depolarizing channel at $p=0.05$, B-RL-S with eight priority levels achieves approximately one fifth the block error rate (BLER) of flooding BP followed by order-10 ordered-statistics decoding. The respective caps are $1000$ sequential iterations for B-RL-S and $1000$ flooding iterations for the BP stage of the reference decoder. These results highlight strong error correction with inexpensive scheduling and no additional post-processing stage.

papers.title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
papers.abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

papers.title: Capillary-gravity wave resistance of a translating, pulsating source
papers.abstract: A disturbance in steady rectilinear translation along a capillary-gravity interface radiates waves only above a minimum speed $c_{min}$, where it experiences a wave resistance; below this threshold it generates no waves, and the response is merely a localised deformation of the interface around the source, free of wave resistance. Modulating the source amplitude at a frequency $Ω$ shifts the forcing to the sideband pair $kV\pmΩ$, where $k$ is the wavenumber and $V$ is the translation speed, opening resonance conditions absent from the steady problem; radiation then sets in below the steady threshold $c_{min}$. Here we derive the mean wave resistance $\langle R\rangle$ of a line source in closed form, and show it to be strictly positive at every nonzero speed $V$: the drag-free below-threshold regime disappears for any $Ω\neq 0$. Crossing the radiation transitions---where the group velocity matches the source speed---produces integrable resonant peaks in $\langle R\rangle$, whose exponents we derive, including at the cusp where two transition branches merge. Below threshold, where a steadily moving source feels no drag, $\langle R\rangle$ rises from zero as $Ω^5$ (at fixed $V$). Throughout, surface tension is essential to $\langle R\rangle$: because it controls the short, dominant capillary-scale waves, discarding it misrepresents $\langle R\rangle$ over almost the entire speed-frequency plane.

papers.title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$Vélez permutation
papers.abstract: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and Vélez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.

papers.title: Epitaxial Oxide Thin Films with High Entropy and Anomalous Crystallinity
papers.abstract: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) expands the compositional and structural possibilities of high-entropy oxide (HEO) thin films through far-from-equilibrium growth and kinetic arrest of metastable configurations. This review connects growth kinetics and epitaxial constraints to the roles of individual cations in shaping the resulting films. We focus primarily on rock salt MgCoNiCuZnO and its derivatives, with selected fluorite, spinel, and perovskite examples illustrating broader applicability. In MgCoNiCuZnO, Co valence and Cu coordination illustrate how chemistry and growth conditions jointly enable lattice tuning and coherent nanostructure formation, while aliovalent and size-misfit additions expand the accessible defect and compositional landscapes. These coupled degrees of freedom underpin anomalous crystallinity, the coexistence of extensive chemical disorder with exceptional crystalline quality and epitaxial order, including full coherence in selected systems, particularly rock salts grown on MgO. This combination opens opportunities to discover and engineer functional configurations in high-quality single-layer films and heterostructures.

papers.title: A Hybrid Gaussian Process-Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine Learning Framework for Robust Knockdown Factor Prediction and Reliability-Based Design of Thin Spherical Shell Caps
papers.abstract: Elastic buckling remains a critical concern in the design of deep spherical shell caps, given that experiments reveal a significant reduction of critical loads from those predicted by linearized eigen-buckling analysis. This discrepancy has been attributed to initial geometric imperfections and is often reconciled through a dimensionless parameter, namely the knockdown factor (KDF). However, conventional KDFs (NASA SP-8007; Eurocode 3) are highly conservative, as they represent the lower bound of an extensive body of experimental data. This study aims to narrow the conservatism in the KDFs for spherical shell caps through machine learning (ML) regression models trained on experimental data on spherical shell buckling. A hybrid model is proposed by combining Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and its improved performance is demonstrated over conventional ML algorithms, i.e., the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), Random Forest Regressor (RFR), and Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGBoost). Each of these models uses six input features and a single output, i.e., the KDF. The most critical feature affecting the KDF is ascertained through a sensitivity analysis. The study concludes with a reliability-based design framework that relies on the predictive ML model to obtain safety-consistent, yet less conservative, KDFs.

papers.title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
papers.abstract: We perform direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence to investigate the mechanisms responsible for the maintenance of large-scale geostrophic vortices. We confirm that the Reynolds stresses generated by inertial waves are consistent with the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes balance of the large-scale flow and demonstrate the predicted cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, with cyclones exhibiting stronger azimuthal velocities and more compact cores. Wave-field analysis provides evidence that geostrophic vortices selectively reflect and absorb inertial waves according to the sign of their angular momentum. Wave absorption occurs either through the formation of a critical layer ahead of the reflection point or through enhanced viscous dissipation associated with increasing local wavenumber. As rotation increases, fewer inertial waves undergo resonant absorption, reducing angular-momentum transfer to the vortices and weakening the geostrophic flow. Consequently, the fraction of energy contained in geostrophic modes depends non-monotonically on the rotation rate, demonstrating that sufficiently rapid rotation can ultimately suppress, rather than enhance, turbulence two-dimensionalization.

papers.title: Personalized LLM Recommendation with Semantic IDs: Autoregressive Beam Search vs. Multi-Token Prediction
papers.abstract: Large-scale personalization is shifting from embedding-table retrieval to LLM-based recommenders that generate the Semantic ID (SID) of the item to recommend, where each SID is a short sequence of discrete hierarchical content codes. A single instruction-tuned model can then unify retrieval, content understanding, and language, and recommend brand-new titles from their content alone using SID; then, how should the model generate the SID? Traditionally, models rely on a single language modeling head that generates tokens autoregressively, typically using constrained beam search. In contrast, an emerging body of work explores multi-token prediction (MTP), where dedicated heads predict all tokens in parallel, substantially reducing the decoding latency associated with beam search. We report an industry-scale, apples-to-apples comparison of these two generation paradigms: single-head autoregressive decoding vs. MTP. We introduce a new auxiliary ranking loss, defined over the joint SID score, to train the MTP objective. We evaluate the SID training objectives on both quality and training/inference cost, inside a multi-task LLM that jointly does personalized retrieval, content question-answering (QA), and instruction following over a large streaming-media catalog. Our experiments show single-head beam search consistently beats MTP on most product-critical metrics: ranking and content QA, and trains at roughly 2.6x lower dollar cost on Qwen3-8B scale; MTP wins only on raw inference throughput. Around this finding, we detail an efficient training and inference stack and report end-to-end gains over the previous non-SID baseline equipped with an auxiliary ranking head: +77% item cold-start ranking, +22% content-QA accuracy, +2.8x faster training, with language metric regression traced to SID vocabulary expansion. We address the language regression by reinforcement learning post training.

papers.title: Penetrating the Reality Wall: Long-Range and Through-Wall AR/VR Privacy Eavesdropping via Wireless Power Side Channel
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, Metaverse technology (AR/VR) has seen widespread adoption in numerous areas, including gaming, social networking, and online collaboration. Although recent studies have exposed vulnerabilities in VR systems, they often apply methods (e.g., pre-installed malicious apps or scripts) from conventional mobile platforms directly, demonstrating impractical attacks that fail to investigate unique privacy leakages specific to VR platforms. In this paper, we present an orthogonal attempt to analyze the attack surface of the power side channel on AR/VR's network connection by capturing the through-wall wireless power in the network transmission medium (e.g., Wi-Fi signals) non-intrusively in a comparatively long distance (e.g., 5.0m-8.0m) and further reconstructing multi-level privacy-aware user behaviors. We propose MetaSpy to validate the feasibility and practicality of our disclosed wireless power-based traffic analysis attack. It first captures through-wall wireless power transmitted from the Wi-Fi router of an adjacent room, identifies the device type, then infers (i) user interactions such as browsing websites, running AR/VR apps, and performing various in-app activities, (ii) unseen VR-specific activities in VR games (e.g., Population: ONE), and (iii) avatar-based user re-identification and virtual keystroke inference corresponding to head movements. We evaluated the effectiveness of MetaSpy in four commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) VR headsets, and the empirical results demonstrate its competitive accuracy in unveiling multi-level user privacy within virtual scenes in through-wall settings at a longer distance (1.8x-80x) than most of the recent studies, and it shows resilience to a series of external interference and impact factors. In addition, we also propose and evaluate effective countermeasures to protect data confidentiality in AR/VR wireless transmission.

papers.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of Kähler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform à priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

papers.title: REFLEX: A Learned On-Board Reflex for Robust Autonomous Collision Recovery of Soft Quadrotors
papers.abstract: Collision-resilient airframes allow quadrotors to survive impacts, but do not ensure autonomous post-collision recovery. Innovation gating in stock onboard estimators often rejects valid external velocity measurements after high-speed impacts, compromising recovery. We present REFLEX, a collision-recovery flight mode that runs entirely on the flight controller, requiring neither contact sensors nor a companion computer. Its proprioceptive recurrent policy stabilizes the vehicle without position, velocity, heading, or altitude estimates. The translational estimate is reinitialized while REFLEX is active, and a trust gate checks estimator consistency before returning control to the stock autopilot. The policy is trained in simulation using proximal policy optimization, with episodes initialized from post-impact states measured in 47 real collisions. In hardware experiments, REFLEX recovered 19 of 22 wall impacts at 5.03 $\pm$ 0.09 m/s, compared with 1 of 14 for the matched stock autopilot. These included 15 consecutive recoveries in a single flight. A separate exploratory flight demonstrated two additional recoveries at 6.02 and 6.05 m/s within the same flight, exceeding the previously reported velocity for autonomous wall-collision recovery by 64%.

papers.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
papers.abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.

papers.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark
papers.abstract: A reading departs from what a monitoring system expects for one of three reasons: the physical process changed, the instrument is failing, or the value was corrupted between the instrument and the software. The three call for different responses and look alike in a single sample. We state the three-cause problem, prove which pairs of causes one channel cannot separate, and propose a bank of online detectors - a Kalman tracker with CUSUM and EWMA charts on its innovation, a Hampel median with generalized-ESD confirmation, a robust noise statistic with ADWIN, exact-value checks and an optional two-channel complementary filter - combined by a deterministic, inspectable attribution rule. The detectors were merged into a public algorithm library. On 2,942 injected events of thirteen fault types the method detects 96.3% (95% interval 95.7-97.0) at 0.22 false alarms per hour and attributes 91.2% (90.6-91.8) of detected events correctly from one channel and 99.0% (98.6-99.4) with a second, rate channel; from one channel only 2 of 207 detected sensor drifts are attributed to the instrument, as the problem statement predicts. Injected into recorded industrial signals, the same catalogue is detected at 80.8% and attributed correctly at 84.5%, at 3.6 false alarms per hour. On the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark the method detects 32 of 33 experiments with a median delay of 15 s, at 46 false alarms per hour against 11 for a rolling z-score.

papers.title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellensätze for free modules.

papers.title: Unchecked or Falsely Accused? Evaluating AI-Generated Text Detectors on Kazakh
papers.abstract: AI-text detectors are already applied to Kazakh writing, yet no study reports how often publicly available detectors flag Kazakh text whose human authorship is dated before ChatGPT. We present AINA-KK: 3,811 human passages from encyclopedic, news, web and educational pages that provably existed before ChatGPT, and 5,597 machine and gray-zone passages from 9 generators, including the Kazakh-built KazLLM and Sherkala, with script and length stress tests. Five English-trained detectors from the Hugging Face Hub flag up to 81.4% of human passages and 79.6% of published student essays; recalibrated, they catch at most 1.3% of machine text. Calibrated zero-shot detectors catch at most 50.3% of machine text from in-distribution generators. Fine-tuned encoders rank text almost perfectly, but mDeBERTa at its default threshold flags 24.4% of 50-word human excerpts, partly because machine outputs are shorter than human text; calibrated, it catches only 47.1% of KazLLM and 62.7% of Sherkala passages. Without script handling, machine-transliterated Latin-2021 text defeats every detector. Fixes that need no new data (calibration, script canonicalization, script-augmented and length-matched training, and an OR with a zero-shot scorer) form AINA-KK-Det. On test it flags 0.9% of human passages (95% CI 0.4-2.7; 1.5% on development data) and catches 85.2% of machine text from known generators, 92.9% from two unseen Gemini-family Gemma-4 models and 61.3% from the Kazakh-built ones; its configuration was chosen with test results in view. We release the data, code and detector at https://github.com/ozxmn/aina-kk.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
papers.abstract: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

papers.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Testing and Automation of Open RAN Systems: GNG-OTA Framework
papers.abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) empower operators with choice and customization through their disaggregated and interoperable architecture. However, ensuring interoperability in O-RAN presents challenges due to complex testing environments and evolving specifications. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing the Generative AI and Graph Neural Network-based Open RAN Testing and Automation (GNG-OTA) framework. GNG-OTA utilizes state-of-the-art AI techniques including generative AI, natural language processing, and graph neural networks to enable accurate, reliable, efficient, and automatic O-RAN interoperability and performance testing.

papers.title: Integration, Enhancements and Evaluation of Memory Simulators
papers.abstract: Currently, there is no common methodology or set of practices for evaluating memory-system performance in integrated simulation infrastructures. As a result, studies adopt different evaluation approaches, which can lead to conflicting conclusions even for the same simulation infrastructure. We propose a validation methodology that evaluates memory-system performance from three complementary views: the memory simulator, the CPU--memory interface and the simulated application. We use these views to detect, understand and correct memory-simulation inaccuracies arising from simulator integration and simplified modeling of microarchitectural features. The methodology reveals that the application's perception of memory performance can become effectively decoupled from the detailed memory simulation. Most importantly, we identify and correct a fundamental memory-model mismatch between delayed-response cycle-accurate memory simulators and ZSim, a representative parallel CPU simulator. We demonstrate the broader applicability of these enhancements by applying them to ZSim integrations with Ramulator 2, DRAMsim3 and DRAMSys 4, covering all major public cycle-accurate memory simulators. After the corrections and enhancements, all integrations reproduce the main bandwidth--latency trends and key characteristics of the actual system. Across the evaluated simulators, STREAM bandwidth differs from actual-hardware measurements by less than 5% in most experiments, while pointer-chase latency remains 15--18% lower than on actual hardware. All simulator enhancements are released as open source.

papers.title: Quantum Localization in Geometric Complex Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum localization, the phenomenon by which wave diffusion is halted, here understood as the superposition of propagating waves, can have many different origins, such as onsite random potentials in Anderson localization. However, some systems exhibit complex geometries and could potentially reproduce similar results without external potentials. In this work, we study how localization of single particle states is affected by the underlying topology of a simple but highly predictive complex network model: the geometric soft configuration model $\mathbb S^1$. By tuning the model's temperature and heterogeneity parameters, we are able to generate different structural patterns and focus on the transition from a small-world to a non-small-world regime. Our study suggests that small-world networks tend to have extended states, which spread the whole system's size, in contrast to non-small-world networks which tend to localize, showing how complex connectivity can play the role assigned to random energetic disorder.

papers.title: Undecidability of Reachability for Constraint Automata
papers.abstract: We prove that reachability for constraint automata over finite binary words is undecidable. Eight registers suffice, with conjunctive guards using only equality, proper prefix, proper suffix, and infix incomparability, without word constants or concatenation. Finite-run nonemptiness, Buechi nonemptiness, and bounded Buechi nonemptiness are undecidable as consequences. For Boolean guards over equality, prefix, suffix, and prefix and suffix incomparability, Buechi nonemptiness is PSPACE-complete with arbitrarily many registers and word constants. The upper bound also allows positive infix atoms and yields PSPACE-completeness of prefix--suffix LTL satisfiability.

papers.title: Scaled three-dimensional simulations of giant-planet accretion and disk clearing
papers.abstract: We develop accelerated three-dimensional simulations of growing planet pairs that draw on a finite gas reservoir. An annulus compression (Scaling A) shortens the predicted clearing time and shrinks the computational domain at equal grid resolution while preserving key physical parameters. Planetary seeds start with Hill radii equal to the disk scale height, retaining three-dimensional accretion. We demonstrate the method in scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System configurations, assuming perfect Hill capture by growing planets on circular orbits. We compare Scaling A at radius-compression factor \(Γ=1.75\) with the unscaled PDS system at matched resolution, through a 1\% reduction of the interplanetary gas inventory. The scaled run is nearly an order of magnitude faster, with similar accreted mass and a comparable partition of gas between the planets. For the Solar-System configuration at \(Γ=3\), the scaling forecasts a speedup of nearly two orders of magnitude at equal local resolution. The scaling is complementary to orbital advection. On eight CPU cores of a desktop computer, the scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System runs reduce the gas inventory between the orbiting planets by roughly half in less than a day. Accretion-driven orbital convergence narrows the shared feeding zone and, together with gas clearing, limits the planetary growth budget. In our scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System runs, the angular momentum carried by meridional inflow directly constrains delivery theory. These results establish a practical route to testing accretion theory against simulations at matched scaled parameters, before applying it to unscaled planetary systems.

papers.title: Fine asymptotics for approximate simulation of symmetric channels
papers.abstract: We study the approximate channel simulation problem in the normal approximation regime. Our starting point is the fact established by Cao et al.~\cite{Cao_channel_simulation}, that the minimal codebook size $M_ε^*(W)$ for a fixed error tolerance $ε>0$ is closely related to the $ε$-smooth channel max-information, $I_{\max}^ε(W)$. Using this, we refine earlier large-blocklength approximations to $M_ε^*(W^{\otimes n})$ for discrete memoryless channels. Specifically, we provide tight third-order expansions for Gallager-symmetric channels and demonstrate that the third-order term is channel-dependent. As in corresponding channel coding expansions, we identify a substantial rate gap between singular and nonsingular channels. Notably, the direction of this gap is reversed relative to channel coding: The third-order term is $-\frac{1}{2}\log n$ for singular channels but $O(\log\log n)$ for nonsingular channels.

papers.title: Multi-GPU Communication Schemes for Iterative Solvers: When CPUs are Not in Charge
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a fully autonomous execution model for multi-GPU applications that completely excludes the involvement of the CPU beyond the initial kernel launch. In a typical multi-GPU application, the host serves as the orchestrator of execution by directly launching kernels, issuing communication calls, and acting as a synchronizer for devices. We argue that this orchestration, or control flow path, causes undue overhead and can be delegated entirely to devices to improve performance in applications that require communication among peers. For the proposed CPU-free execution model, we leverage existing techniques such as persistent kernels, thread block specialization, device-side barriers, and device-initiated communication routines to write fully autonomous multi-GPU code and achieve significantly reduced communication overheads. We demonstrate our proposed model on two broadly used iterative solvers, 2D/3D Jacobi stencil and Conjugate Gradient(CG). Compared to the CPU-controlled baselines, the CPU-free model can improve 3D stencil communication latency by 58.8% and provide a 1.63x speedup for CG on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The project code is available at https://github.com/ParCoreLab/CPU-Free-model.

papers.title: End-to-End Fidelity and Rate Analysis for Zero-Added-Loss Multiplexing
papers.abstract: Zero-added-loss multiplexing (ZALM)~[Phys. Rev. Appl. {\bf 19}, 054029 (2023)] is a midpoint-source scheme for entanglement distribution. Its quantum transmitter (QTX) employs two Sagnac sources of polarization-entangled pairs plus partial Bell-state measurements (BSMs) on their idler outputs to herald entanglement in their signal outputs, thus avoiding the switching losses suffered by other multiplexing approaches. When its Sagnac sources' spontaneous parametric downconverters (SPDCs) utilize $χ^{(2)}$ crystals with phase-matched spectral islands, ZALM avoids the tradeoff between heralding efficiency and output-state fidelity incurred when conventional-crystal SPDCs' outputs are channelized by dense wavelength-division multiplexing filters. This paper reports an end-to-end fidelity and rate analysis for islands-based ZALM that includes: SPDC multipair emissions of all orders and partial-BSM losses in the ZALM QTX; loss in propagation from the ZALM QTX to Alice and Bob's quantum receivers (QRXs); loss and mode mismatch in the mode converters employed at Alice and Bob's QRXs; and loss in the partial-BSM loading of Alice and Bob's emissive quantum memories.

papers.title: From Lyapunov Growth to Weak Quantum Chaos
papers.abstract: Local out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) measure the growth of initially small commutators. For bounded local operators, this growth ends when the local commutator becomes of order one, but in an extended system the region over which it is large can continue to expand. We study this spatial proliferation using three related observables: the local squared commutator $C_r(t)$, its spatial sum $\bar C(t) = \sum_r C_r(t)$, and the symmetrically regularised connected dOTOC $D(t)$ of two extensive observables. We show that Lieb--Robinson locality gives $\bar C(t) \lesssim t^d$. We then prove that, in a Gibbs state with uniform exponential clustering, the full dOTOC obeys the same bound, $D(t) \lesssim t^d$, improving our earlier suboptimal $t^{3d}$ bound. We illustrate these results in two quantum many-body systems: a Brownian coupled-cluster model and a finite-temperature SYK chain. In both cases, an exact disorder symmetry relates $D(t)$ to $\bar C(t)$ and allows us to follow the same extensive observable from the pre-scrambling Lyapunov regime into the post-scrambling growth associated with an expanding saturated region. This late-time power-law growth is the concrete realisation of the weak quantum chaos introduced in our earlier work.

papers.title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and the failure of Fourier-Schur transference
papers.abstract: Given $1 < p < \infty$ and a function $m \colon \mathbf{N}_0 \to \mathbf{C}$, we provide a characterization of radial Schur multipliers $M(x,y) = m(d(x,y))$ on the Schatten $p$-class of a tree $(X,d)$ equipped with its graph metric. That is, the operator norm of the radial Schur multiplier $S_M$ is controlled by the norm of the Fourier multiplier $T_m$ on the torus: \[ \big\| S_M \colon S_p(X) \to S_p(X) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}} \lesssim \frac{p^4}{(p-1)^2} \, \big\| T_m \colon L_p(\mathbf{T}) \to L_p(\mathbf{T}) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}}, \] with both quantities being comparable when the tree $X$ has infinite diameter. This is a rather unexpected inequality, which necessarily fails at the endpoints $p=1,\infty$ due to the work of Haagerup, Steenstrup and Szwarc. As an application, we construct the first examples of completely $S_p$-bounded Herz-Schur multipliers in the free group that are unbounded as Fourier multipliers. This result disproves Fourier-Schur transference---a longstanding open problem since the work of Neuwirth and Ricard in 2011. In line with this, our main result also implies the surprising fact that free balls Schur multipliers are uniformly $S_p$-bounded, in sharp contrast to their Fourier behavior. In addition, we disprove Fourier-Schur transference over the algebraic groups $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbf{Q}_q)$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$ with $\mathrm{K}$-biinvariant counterexamples, the latter involving additional geometric and probabilistic techniques.

papers.title: Low-rank perturbation of symplectic matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

papers.title: Engram Injection: A Study of Temporal Validity in Parametric Language-Model Memory
papers.abstract: A stored fact may stop being valid when a user changes a preference or an event replaces an earlier one. We study whether a language model can learn these changes in its parameters and answer correctly from only a question and the current time. Engram Injection stores facts in LoRA adapters and supplies the clock through FiLM conditioning on a frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct model. We compare it with additive clock conditioning, prompting with the full dated history, and retrieving four dated records. We train six matched adapters across three seeds after fixing a sampler that could admit test-age examples into training. The training audit reports no such examples among 127,760 evaluated training inputs. On 62 pairs of questions asked before and after an update, at an elapsed age of seven days excluded from training, both adapter methods answer zero pairs correctly under the primary blinded assistant review with order code 1 held fixed. Full-history prompting answers 59/62 pairs correctly, and retrieval answers 62/62. Separate experiments show that adapters can store facts and that removable memory units can support local deletion. Combining fact selection with time-based version selection remains unsuccessful. These results separate learning a fact from learning when to use it.

papers.title: What the Model Cannot See: Covert and Provable Text Invisibility in LLMs
papers.abstract: Text wrapped in a trigger can be made behaviorally invisible to a language model: omitted from summaries and quotations, ignored in question answering, and left unflagged by downstream filtering. We study this selective blindness as a dual-use information-flow primitive, a supply-chain backdoor, and a white-box auditing problem. We first implement it exactly as a serving-time span veto: blocking information flow out of a marked span makes every outside activation bit-identical under same-length substitution of the span's content, a noninterference property we verify across ten models, seven mixer families, and 0.5B-120B parameters. The veto serves as a deployable quarantine, an exact reference for calibrating leakage, and a teacher. Distilled into weights, it yields a backdoor: checkpoints trained on six model families from 4B to 120B ignore marked context at little benchmark cost, and their outputs show no measurable semantic trace of the suppressed content above the veto reference on our held-out suite; an in-domain variant suppresses planted vulnerabilities during AI code review. Detection is therefore a white-box problem. Simpler backdoors remain internally transparent -- linear probes recover suppressed content at 0.57-0.79 accuracy versus 0.025 chance -- but hardening the attack until probes reach chance collapses attention from outside the span into it below the range of base models. Across the attacks we evaluate, probe visibility trades off against routing visibility; we do not establish that this tradeoff is fundamental.

papers.title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use
papers.abstract: LLM agents that call external tools must decide what to do when a tool call times out: retrying risks duplicate side effects, while not retrying can leave the task incomplete. We present RetryBench, an evaluation protocol for retry decisions and failure recovery in tool-using LLM agents. Each decision is scored on retry permission (is the retry justified by an idempotency-key guarantee or proof of non-execution?), settled effects (duplicates and omissions), and completion, by replaying it across all hidden execution worlds consistent with the observation. On four synthetic software-engineering tasks, we run two controlled prompt-sensitivity studies (1,728 decisions). Study 1 (idempotency-key descriptions): with the contract fixed, GPT-5.6 Luna reuses the valid idempotency key in 10/40 decisions when an extra key is described as a "Candidate recovery key" but in 39/40 when it is an "Alternative key string"; across three further phrasings per family the gap is 27/120 versus 113/120. GPT-5.6 Sol and Terra are at ceiling (40/40). Study 2 (action order): under underspecified lookup guarantees, retry rates are 17-27 points lower for GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-5.4 when retry is listed first (option-order bias), mainly on two tasks; we make no claim about which behavior is better. Findings are limited to researcher-chosen phrasings, four tasks and unpinned model aliases. Code and all model responses are released.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions
papers.abstract: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is computationally expensive for iterative building design. Deep learning surrogates offer faster predictions, but generalization across varying room dimensions remains challenging. This study compares two geometry-conditioned neural network surrogate models for rapid indoor airflow and temperature field prediction under varying room sizes. During the architectural design stage, this method is relevant for real-time assessment of whether conditioned supply air will effectively provide fresh and cool air throughout rooms with varying heights and lengths. The canvas-based neural network (CaNN) explicitly encodes room size by preserving different occupied regions within a fixed canvas, whereas the coordinate-based neural network (CoNN) uses normalized coordinate channels. Both employ U-Net autoencoders to separately predict airflow and temperature fields. Evaluation uses simplified rooms with varying heights and lengths as a controlled benchmark. The results show that CaNN achieves higher agreement with CFD results than CoNN, demonstrating its potential to support performance-driven building design.

papers.title: Learning based Scalable Multi-Objective Scheduling of Workflows across UD-IaaS-FaaS Systems
papers.abstract: Workflow scheduling in user device-centric edge-cloud computing has emerged as a challenging problem due to the need to jointly optimize execution performance, energy consumption, and monetary cost. Modern workflows consist of heterogeneous tasks, where compute-intensive components are well-suited for Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) resources, while fine-grained, event-driven tasks are more efficiently executed using the Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) model. We formulate this scheduling problem for application workflows over a hybrid User Device (UD)-IaaS-FaaS computing continuum as a multi-objective Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP). The formulation models the workflow execution mechanism by incorporating cumulative capacity constraints for IaaS resources and elastic resource provisioning for FaaS. To overcome the intractability of MILP, we propose a learning-based framework that combines graph neural networks, surrogate performance modeling, and a multi-sample REINFORCE approach. The proposed approach is workflow-aware, leveraging task pairing to improve data locality and structured task placement decisions. Agent training is organized into three stages: small-scale learning of UD-IaaS trade-offs, intermediate locality aware co-location, and large-scale handling of parallelism and aggregation bottlenecks in workflows. The proposed framework is validated through real-world experiments using the Pegasus Montage workflow on a custom UD-IaaS-FaaS testbed comprising a user device, multiple IaaS nodes, and serverless FaaS instances. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the improved trade-offs across makespan, energy consumption, and cost. Compared with the genetic algorithm and greedy scheduling approaches, the proposed approach reduces makespan by 10-17.5%, energy consumption by 3-9%, and cost by 4-10%, while remaining within 3.5-5.6% of the MILP optimum.

papers.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
papers.abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellensätze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

papers.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
papers.abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.

papers.title: Variance-Optimal State Resampling for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards spends much of its rollout budget on states that yield no learning signal. We recast this as a question about the sampling distribution itself: under a fixed rollout budget, which distribution over states minimizes the variance of the policy-gradient estimator? The answer admits a closed-form Neyman allocation, $μ_{\mathrm{var}}^π(s) \propto d^π(s)\,σ_π(s)$, which connects naturally to GRPO's group-relative advantage and induces an emergent reverse curriculum as the policy improves, with no externally imposed schedule. Building on this principle, we propose VSR (Variance-driven State Resampling), a plug-in modification to GRPO using a prefix replay buffer and a zero-cost variance proxy. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks and long-horizon agentic tasks (Sokoban, BabyAI), VSR outperforms GRPO and GiGPO on most benchmarks with fewer generated tokens per update.

papers.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
papers.abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.

papers.title: Lack of exponential stability for thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that the classical thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with thermal coupling acting only on the bending moment are not exponentially stable under full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions if the equal wave speed condition is not satisfied. Combined with their well-known converses, our results provide complete characterizations of exponential stability in terms of the coefficients of each system. To the best of our knowledge, these characterizations were previously known only under mixed boundary conditions. The proof is based on the introduction of a boundary correction term in the standard trigonometric ansatz so that the full homogeneous Dirichlet conditions are satisfied.

papers.title: O-SCOPE: a Raspberry Pi Pico oscilloscope
papers.abstract: In this paper we provide an introduction to some of the efficient features of the Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2) family of microconroller boards (RP2040 and RP2350). More exactly, we show how to use PIO (Programmable Input/Output) and DMA (Direct Memory Access) to program the RP2 boards for efficient DAC (Digital to Analog) and ADC (Analog to Digital) conversions. Using OP-AMPS (Operational Amplifiers) we also show how to build a minimal electronic frontend interface for signal input/output. Finally, we integrate all these components into a product, the O-SCOPE, which is a practical and easy to use oscilloscope and wave function generator. The RP2 component of the O-SCOPE is built using Micropython, while the user interface is developed using vanilla Javascript and it runs on the web browser of any computer, interacting with the RP2 board via the Web Serial API. The O-SCOPE web interface is hosted on GitHub Pages such that it is directly accessible everywhere using a web browser, such that no local installation is required. Also, the RP2 software component is freely distributed on GitHub using the UF2 (USB Flashing Format) mass storage file, and it can be installed by simply dragging the file on the RP2 boards. These features make the O-SCOPE easily accessible, transforming it into a very low cost and useful tool for laboratories everywhere in the world.

papers.title: Learning Multimodal Sensor Fusion with JEPA Representations for Breathing Activity and Pose Recognition
papers.abstract: Predictive video representations do not by themselves specify how a multimodal system should handle missing sensors. We transfer frozen V-JEPA2 features to a set of heterogeneous sensors comprised by RGB video, depth video, and radar time series. A shared fusion model uses modality queries, fixed sensor slots, and explicit availability to classify breathing activity and pose from all seven non-empty sensor subsets. The contribution is a controlled evaluation of subset supervision, pooling capacity, and representation transfer on 39 OMuSense-23 subjects with five subject-group folds and three seeds. With matched downstream parameter counts, the final model reaches recording-level activity macro-F1 of $75.23%\pm0.60$ averaged across seven subsets. Supervising all subsets in each batch improves the matched query-pooling control by 1.923 percentage points (conditional 95% subject-bootstrap interval [0.647, 3.209]), while query pooling shows no clear advantage over matched mean pooling under balanced supervision. Radar probes support transfer beyond pooled wavelet pixels, 64-token inference approximately preserves mean activity performance, and the tested Consensus-JEPA loss adds no measured benefit against its exact control.

papers.title: Minimax Rates and Improved Spectral Convergence for Multi-Manifold Clustering
papers.abstract: We study eigenpair estimation for the tensorized, density-weighted Laplace--Beltrami operator from $n$ independent data points sampled from a multi-manifold mixture distribution where manifolds may intersect. Let $d$ denote the largest intrinsic dimension of the manifold components and $s\geq2$ the smoothness of the sampling densities. For simple, nontrivial eigenpairs, we establish the minimax rate $n^{-s/(d+2s)}$ for approximating the eigenvalue and eigenfunction of the tensorized Laplace--Beltrami operator, and show that a continuum plug-in estimator based on kernel density estimation attains the same rate when the supporting manifolds are known. We further analyze a manifold-agnostic graph Laplacian estimator and prove that its eigenpairs converge to those of the tensorized Laplace--Beltrami operator at rate $n^{-1/(2.5d-1)}$, up to logarithmic factors, improving upon previously known spectral convergence rates for multi-manifold learning. Numerical experiments on synthetic multi-manifold data corroborate the rates guaranteed by our theorems. These results characterize the information-theoretic difficulty of multi-manifold spectral estimation and quantify the additional cost of learning without oracle component information.

papers.title: Forensic Analysis of the HackRF One with PortaPack Mayhem Firmware
papers.abstract: Software-defined radios (SDRs) have become an inexpensive, portable platform for replay attacks, location spoofing and jamming. The HackRF One can operate stand-alone when fitted with a PortaPack interface board running the open-source Mayhem firmware. No peer-reviewed study has addressed the forensic analysis of this device family. This work establishes, at source-code level, where forensically relevant data reside on the microSD card of a device running Mayhem v2.0.1, in which format, when they are written and how they should be interpreted. The methodology is applied to an SD card image that the author acquired from their own device after four months of real use, and every inference is drawn from the image alone. The workflow covers timestamp rules that depend on the real-time clock (RTC) battery state, traces of on-device trimming and text editing, cluster-level recovery of deleted in-phase/quadrature (IQ) captures, and decoding of recorded signals cross-checked with an independent decoder. In the example image, the final part of a deleted IQ capture and a trimmed-away capture segment are recovered, and six captures are attributed to a single rolling-code on-off keying (OOK) transmitter sharing one 32-bit identifier. The study provides practitioners with an artifact catalogue, interpretation rules and acquisition recommendations.

papers.title: Local-dimension-invariant low-density parity-check stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: The protection of quantum information in systems leveraging more than two basis states (qudits) is an ongoing challenge. A tool for transforming the plethora of qubit stabilizer codes into qudit stabilizer codes is the local-dimension-invariant (LDI) extension to the stabilizer formalism. A drawback of the LDI method is that generally in order to ensure the distance of the resultant code is at least preserved the newly selected local-dimension will need to be any prime bigger than a large cutoff value. In this work we consider the repercussions of this large cutoff value, then by focusing on quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes we are able to bring down this cutoff value. Notably, we are able to reduce it in some cases to the initial local-dimension and for arbitrary CSS qubit-derived codes to singly exponential in $d$ with no dependence on the number of logicals $k$. This reduces the size of the caveat in LDI forms in their distance preservation condition.

papers.title: Make Every Expansion Count: Learning to Search Efficiently in LLM Code Repair
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) code-repair systems fix faulty programs by repeatedly generating and testing revisions. Each revision is costly, making the choice of which repair to pursue important for efficiency. Existing search policies rely on test pass rates and search statistics, ignoring the details of test failures and proposed edits. We introduce CodeTriage, a learned policy that prioritizes edits before their revised programs are generated and tested. Its 0.6B-parameter model reads the test output, failure diagnosis, and proposed edit, then predicts a distribution over the number of repair steps needed to reach a fix through that edit. These predictions prioritize all pending edits across programs before generating and testing the revised code. On held-out repair tasks, CodeTriage finds fixes with 21% fewer program revisions and 12% fewer output tokens than the strongest baseline on each metric. Without retraining, it achieves the highest average success across search budgets for each of 11 unseen repair LLMs. Ablations show that both the failure context and edit text, as well as comparisons across programs, improve search. We also release a corpus of 12.2 million program versions from four LLMs, organized into repair trees with proposed edits and test results.

papers.title: Assessing the impact of background subtraction on a dust-free corona
papers.abstract: Context. White-light observations of the solar corona contain contributions from both the electron-scattered K-corona and the dust-scattered F-corona. Because the diffuse F-corona dominates the measured intensity at altitudes of approximately 4 $R_{\odot}$ and above, background subtraction techniques are routinely employed to isolate the electron corona in coronagraph observations. Aims. Since no direct observational "ground truth" for the K-corona exists, the amount of coronal signal that is inadvertently removed by background subtraction methods remains unknown. We aim to quantify, for the first time, the impact of background subtraction on the inferred large-scale structure and brightness of the solar corona. Methods. We use a 32-day simulation based on a novel near-real-time, data-assimilative, time-evolving magnetohydrodynamic model to generate synthetic white-light observables. Because these synthetic observations are free from dust and instrumental stray-light contributions, they provide direct access to the "true" K-corona and enable a quantitative assessment of the effects of background subtraction. Results. We find that background subtraction generally preserves the large-scale morphology of the electron corona, including the locations and shapes of major coronal structures. However, the procedure systematically modifies the relative brightness of different features and removes a non-negligible fraction of the K-coronal signal. Conclusions. Although standard background subtraction techniques successfully recover the overall appearance of the electron corona, they can alter its quantitative photometric properties. These findings should be considered when interpreting coronal brightness measurements and deriving physical properties from processed white-light observations.

papers.title: Social Learning of Ranking: Getting the Top Right despite Local Herding
papers.abstract: In sequential learning, a group of agents sequentially receives a noisy private signal and observes the predictions of prior agents to estimate a hidden ground truth. While extensively studied for binary signals, we formalize and analyze sequential learning when the hidden ground truth is an ordering of $n$ items, and both private signals and inferences involve pairwise comparisons. A key focus in sequential learning is herding, where agents disregard their private signals to follow the crowd. We show that, while local herding in our model may lead agents to make incorrect pairwise inferences, the global hidden order can still be approximated. Specifically, by aggregating all pairwise comparison outputs, the highest-ranked items can be retrieved. We investigate top-$k$ retrieval across three scenarios: (1) passive aggregation, where information is gathered from the social learning process without intervention; (2) strategic selection, where agents choose their pairwise comparisons dynamically; and (3) aggregation with stubborn nodes, where a very small set of stubborn agents, who base their inferences solely on their private signals, join the mechanism. With query complexity as the number of agents needed for a high-probability estimation, we propose top-$k$ retrieval algorithms with query complexities sublinear in $O(n^2)$, the total number of pairs.

papers.title: Ordinary and measurable colorings of Euclidean three-space
papers.abstract: A proper coloring of Euclidean space is a coloring that assigns different colors to points at distance one. Using the planar character-law rigidity theorem of OpenAI, we prove that every finite proper coloring of $\R^3$ can be replaced by a proper Lebesgue-measurable coloring with the same number of colors. As a corollary we obtain that the ordinary and measurable chromatic numbers of $\R^3$ are equal, and both lie between $7$ and $15$.

papers.title: Review Rarely Beats the Stronger Model: Separating Verification from Capability Transfer in LLM Pipelines
papers.abstract: Qwen3-8B reviewing Llama-3.1-8B in math adds 33.2 points, yet Qwen3-8B alone is 6.4 points more accurate than the result. Reviewing another model's answer is usually judged by its gain over the generator. We show that this confuses verification, which adds accuracy beyond either model alone, with capability transfer, where a stronger reviewer supplies answers it could have given on its own. Measured against the stronger model alone, across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models (3B to 72B) in math, knowledge, code and reasoning, review beats it in only 9 of 96 review directions, and does worse the larger the capability gap. The reason is anchoring: the reviewer mostly follows the generator, discarding its own correct answers. Review costs 2.6 to 2.8 times as much as the stronger model alone, while a selector using the same two calls is 2.7 to 4.2 points more accurate than review and cheaper. Studies of verification should report the stronger model alone, not only the gain over the generator.

papers.title: Simultaneous Recovery of Dielectric Constants, Photoelastic Constants, and Strain Profiles from Picosecond Ultrasonic Echoes
papers.abstract: Light reflected from a deforming solid depends on boundary motion and strain-induced modulation of the dielectric response. For a propagating acoustic field, scattering from different depths interferes coherently, so the measured optical amplitude and phase depend jointly on the strain profile, dielectric constant, and photoelastic constant. Optical tomography often makes such reconstructions tractable through independent projections. To probe mechanical strain, however, the optical measurement also depends on the material properties that mediate its observation, requiring those properties to be known or assumptions about the field. Here we show that broadband picosecond ultrasonic echoes in an opaque solid can supply the missing information. Fourier transformation of the measured complex relative reflectance change obtained with monochromatic light at normal incidence gives access to many acoustic frequency components. We recover the complex dielectric and photoelastic constants together with the nanoscale depth-dependent strain profile by formulating the reconstruction as a multiparameter nonlinear eigenvalue problem. We demonstrate the method using experimental echoes from a chromium film. The recovered refractive index agrees with ellipsometry, whereas the recovered strain profile closely follows a two-temperature-model prediction including electron and thermal diffusion and frequency-dependent ultrasonic attenuation. Synthetic echoes test robustness to added noise. Broadband response thus replaces additional optical projections, making the measurement self-calibrating and enabling simultaneous recovery of an unknown physical field and the material properties that mediate its optical observation.

papers.title: Lightweight Scheduling Policies for Continuously Batched LLM Serving Across GPU Architectures
papers.abstract: Large language model serving is increasingly limited not only by model size and GPU speed, but also by scheduling during autoregressive decoding, where continuous batching interleaves requests at token granularity as sequences arrive and finish. We study whether lightweight scheduling policies can improve latency-throughput tradeoffs without changing model architectures, kernels, or deploying learned schedulers. We implement a Python/PyTorch continuous-batching testbench with real Hugging Face execution and evaluate eight policies across 1,152 GPU-model-scheduler-workload runs using ShareGPT-derived traffic, six Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral models, and Modal L40S, A100, and H100 GPUs. Scheduler choice changes throughput, TTFT, completion latency, and tail behavior under fixed model, GPU, workload, batch size, and prefill budget. Aging shortest-prompt-first is the strongest practical baseline in many L40S and mixed-workload settings, while oracle remaining-length scheduling shows that job-size knowledge alone is insufficient because batching and hardware effects also shape performance. The custom dataset has been uploaded to Hugging Face.

papers.title: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion
papers.abstract: We present Gen Through the Lens, a camera-controllable image-to-video generation framework that synthesizes videos from a given reference image while enabling realistic and physically consistent camera operations. Unlike previous models that treat camera motion as abstract conditioning or rely on a single coordinate system, our approach explicitly decomposes and fuses control signals across three coordinate spaces: the camera coordinate (modeled by intrinsic parameters), the world coordinate (represented by spatial geometry hints), and the object coordinate (described by 3D bounding boxes of target subjects). Through cross-coordinate conditioning fusion, these heterogeneous cues are unified to guide the generative process, enabling precise control of camera motion, focus, and framing while preserving temporal and spatial coherence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method produces controllable and visually consistent results across diverse camera operations, outperforming existing approaches in both realism and editability.

papers.title: The DAWN JWST Archive: A spectroscopically-informed population study of the physical properties of galaxies at z>2
papers.abstract: Charting the evolution of star-formation, stellar mass and dust build-up over cosmic time relies on the accurate characterisation of the stellar population properties of high redshift galaxies. We present a catalogue of spectroscopically derived physical properties for ~12,000 galaxies at z>2, with archival JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy and JWST/NIRCam imaging from the DAWN JWST Archive. We present a custom version of the SED fitting code BAGPIPES, used to perform joint spectrophotometric modelling of PRISM spectra and broadband NIRCam photometry. In doing so, we publicly release a science-ready catalogue of the physical properties of galaxies beyond cosmic noon. We report key physical properties, such as stellar masses, star-formation rates (SFR) and timescales, and V-band dust attenuation (Av). We further probe the recent star-formation histories (SFH) of galaxies via their SFRs on 3 Myr, 10 Myr, and 100 Myr timescales, capturing both rising and falling recent SFHs. Through dust-corrected ugi colour-colour diagrams of massive galaxies, we show how quiescent and dusty galaxies populate this colour space at z>2, with galaxies experiencing a recent downturn in star-formation occupying distinct parameter space. We also study the dustiest galaxies in our sample, showing that they are preferentially more massive and strongly star-forming relative to the parent sample, residing on the high-mass end of the star-forming main-sequence. The slope of the attenuation curve has a strong dependence on Av, varying from steep to shallow as the dust attenuation increases and the specific star-formation rate decreases. Our findings show that the unparalleled number statistics of this catalogue of spectroscopically derived stellar population properties uniquely enables the study star-formation, quenching and dust properties of galaxies from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn.

papers.title: Forensic Text Recovery from Document Thumbnails Using Text-Aware U-Net
papers.abstract: Forensic analysis of low-resolution Word thumbnails presents a significant challenge because these artifacts may constitute the only remaining visual evidence of deleted documents. Standard Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tools perform poorly on such severely degraded images, creating a critical bottleneck in forensic evidence recovery. Although deep learning architectures, such as U-Net, can improve visual image quality, models optimized solely using pixel-based loss functions tend to favor visual smoothness over the structural fidelity required for accurate text recognition. To address this limitation, we propose a text-aware restoration framework designed for forensic triage. The proposed approach employs a U-Net architecture guided by a hybrid optimization strategy that integrates pixel-level fidelity with machine-readable text constraints. Specifically, an OCR-based Normalized Levenshtein Distance (NLD) metric is used during model selection to prioritize the recovery of an accurate character topology. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the NLD, enabling reliable recovery of machine-readable text from severely degraded thumbnails.

papers.title: BRQGen: Towards Adaptive Completeness Assessment and Follow-Up Question Generation for Bug Reports
papers.abstract: Many bug reports lack the necessary information required to reproduce issues. In early studies, large language models have been employed to generate follow-up questions to enhance incomplete reports. However, they ask a fixed number of questions regardless of whether the report is incomplete. We propose BRQGen, an iterative framework that identifies missing or ambiguous information in bug reports and generates targeted follow-up questions, only if necessary. Reports with no identified gaps are classified as sufficient. When the author responds, BRQGen evaluates whether the answers provide the requested information and generates further questions for any exposed gaps. We curated a novel dataset of 429 incomplete bug reports from Home Assistant and Brave Browser, each containing at least one maintainer follow-up question. Each question is mapped to the author's answer and assigned a label indicating whether the requested information could have been provided directly through the issue template. Earlier maintainer requests were associated with author responses, whereas delayed requests were associated with no response. Among responding authors, requests within one hour received median replies after 0.52 hours in Home Assistant and 1.45 hours in Brave, versus 9.76 and 13.49 hours after four hours. BRQGen covered 35.4% (Qwen 3.8 Flash) to 51.8% (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) of the 1,073 ground-truth follow-up questions. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash managed to ask 45.7% of all detailed questions and 63.9% of all generic questions. Gemini 3 Flash Preview reached the highest macro-F1 for completeness assessment of 49.3%, but with a post-hoc analysis by getting only the gaps with high severities, Qwen 3.8 Flash reaches 73.6% macro-F1 score. Completeness assessment improved when at least one identified gap had high severity, and nearly all ground-truth questions were captured within the first two iterations.
